name: Agenda
description:
1. You asked for a Google-Calendar-style agenda/calendar manager for codx-junior — multiple calendars, notifications with popup reminders, and a `codx-junior` calendar showing scheduled tasks/meets/events (tasks allowed in several calendars) — with deep analysis and a prototype before any code changes.
2. I mapped the platform's existing pieces (meets, events manager, notifications, kanban planning, SQLAlchemy stores, global-settings path convention) and wrote `design/06-calendar/01-analysis.md` (~930 lines, 17 sections incl. storage, API, data model, UX and risks).
3. I built a self-contained clickable prototype (`02-prototype/index.html`, no build/CDN) with month/week/day/agenda views, multi-calendar membership, reminders and notification panel, and verified it in the shared browser — fixing real bugs found on the way.
4. You then settled four open questions: the calendar is **global** across projects with filters, calendars can be **private or team/group**, D3 confirmed, and **no Google integration** now — I propagated those as D1–D4 through the analysis, prototype, fixture and README.
5. Deliverables live under `design/06-calendar/` (analysis, prototype, `calendar-fixture.json` v2 with test assertions, README); **no application code was changed** — implementation starts only when you approve the design.

messages.content:
We need and agenda/calendar  manager where to visualize eventts and planification. We can follow google calendar. w'll be able to create multiple calendars like in google calendar. We'll need notifications section and popup reminders. Probably we'll need a "codx-junior" calendar where we can see scheduled task (we'll need to allow tasks to be in multtiple calendars), meet and events, ...

Create deep analisys and prototype before any changes

I'll start by mapping the project to understand how the platform is structured, then dig into the relevant subsystems.The atlas index is partial, so let me inspect the structure directly.Good — I can already see there's an existing `meets` subsystem, an `events` manager, notifications components, a `SolopreneurCalendar.vue`, and kanban planning. Let me read the key ones.Now the storage and wiring layers: how data is persisted, how tasks model dates, and how views/routes/apps are registered.Now the wiring: router registration in FastAPI, the app component map, and one API module as a pattern reference.Two facts I must verify before proposing an implementation: available date/time libraries and how background services register.I have enough evidence. Now I'll write the deliverables — analysis first, then the interactive prototype.Now the interactive prototype — a single self-contained HTML file (no build step, no CDN, opens offline).Now let me verify the prototype actually works — a prototype with a broken script is worthless.Found two real bugs (hour slots all stacked at the top; Day view showed Monday instead of the cursor day) plus a reminder-toast storm on load. Fixing all three.Both anomalies came from restored localStorage. Let me apply two more improvements (richer seeded history, correct weekday label in Day view) and reload cleanly.Structure verified. Now a functional probe of the interactions (create, multi-calendar, toggle, next-reminder):Let me correct the fixture's expected values — hand-computed counts must be exactly right if tests will assert them.Done — analysis + working prototype, **no application code changed**.

## Delivered (`design/06-calendar/`)

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `01-analysis.md` | The deep analysis (~800 lines, 17 sections + file map) |
| `02-prototype/index.html` | Clickable, self-contained prototype (no build, no CDN) |
| `02-prototype/README.md` | 5-minute tour + the list of deliberate simplifications |
| `03-fixtures/calendar-fixture.json` | Canonical dataset in API shape + expected query/reminder assertions for tests |

Prototype is open in the shared browser: **http://gbrian.codxjunior.com/browser/cff70128-983b-43b4-bf0c-9adf807c1d1a/**

## The decisions that matter

- **Storage**: `<codx_path>/calendar/` (JSON, atomic `tmp`+`os.replace`, `flock`, month shards) — copying `orchestration/store.py`. Events do *not* go into the chat/board document: boards rewrite wholesale on every card move, and tasks must stay single-writer.
- **Multiple calendars without duplication**: the **item owns `calendar_ids[]`**, not the calendar. "Sprint 42 review" is one task with two memberships → one occurrence, two colours.
- **`codx-junior` is a virtual, read-only projection** of `Chat`/runs/meets. Dragging a task chip writes the **task** through the planning API, so we never get a second source of truth.
- **`due_date` stays a deadline**; a new `scheduled_start/end` is the time block. Conflating them would break the tested overdue logic in `planning_manager.py`.
- **Server returns occurrences, not events** (recurrence + timezone expanded once, capped) — precedent already exists in planning. The browser never does date maths.
- **Reminders**: background thread in `background.py` → 30 s tick → `delivered.json` dedupe → socket broadcast → notification centre + popup. Same "exactly once, survives restart" pattern as the harness notification test. Popup = present, centre = record (old ones land flagged *missed*).
- **Google**: ICS export → ICS import → read-only Google → two-way, in that order. Two-way in M0 would sink the milestone (§10 lists why).

## Verified, not just written

Found and fixed 3 real bugs while testing: hour slots collapsed to the top of the week grid, Day view showed Monday instead of the cursor day, and a reminder-toast storm on reload. Final state: month 40 chips · week 9 blocks · day `Thursday, 12 November 2026` 3 blocks · agenda 30 rows; recurrence output matches the fixture exactly (5 standups, offsite/flight correctly excluded); 1 popup on load, older reminder marked *missed*; create with two calendars + reminder persists. Fixture JSON validated (6 calendars, 7 events, 0 dangling ids).

## Before M0 can start — 4 decisions (§17)

1. Calendars **per project** only, or also installation-wide?
2. Are **`personal` calendars private per user**, or everything project-visible? (decides per-user partitioning)
3. Is the calendar the place to **schedule** a meet ahead of time? (note: `MeetManager` is in-memory only — meets vanish on restart; the calendar event would fix that for free)
4. Is Google **read** enough for v1, or required write?

Two honest dependencies I verified: `python-dateutil` and `icalendar` are **not** in `api/pyproject.toml` — M3 needs them added (both pure-Python, MIT).

Want me to turn M0 (§16) into task cards / an orchestration run on the board, or adjust the design first?

```py api/codx/junior/meets/model.py
"""
Data models for the Meets subsystem (WebRTC call management).

A *meet* represents a single call session. Each meet tracks:

* its participants (``MeetParticipant``),
* the WebRTC signalling messages exchanged between them (``MeetSignal``),
* and lifecycle metadata (status, timestamps, initiator).

Diagram:
```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Meet {
        +str meet_id
        +str name
        +str initiator
        +MeetStatus status
        +List~MeetParticipant~ participants
        +List~MeetSignal~ signals
    }
    class MeetParticipant {

class ChatAttachment(BaseModel):
    """Represents a media file (image or audio note) attached to a chat or message,

    file_name: str = Field(description="Original file name of the attachment")
    file_type: str = Field(description="MIME type (e.g., 'image/png', 'audio/webm')")

    @validator('file_size')
    def validate_file_size(cls, v):
        if v > MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE_BYTES:
            raise ValueError(f"Attachment size exceeds maximum allowed size of {MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE_MB}MB")
        return v
    
    @validator('file_type')
    def validate_file_type(cls, v):
        # `MediaRecorder` reports the recording type together with its codec list

        media_type = (v or '').split(';')[0].strip().lower()
        if media_type not in ALLOWED_ATTACHMENT_TYPES:

# Agenda / Calendar Manager — deep analysis

> Status: **design + prototype only. No application code has been changed.**
> Scope: a Google-Calendar-style agenda in codx-junior — multiple calendars, a
> system `codx-junior` calendar fed by scheduled tasks, a notification centre
> and popup reminders.
>
> Companion files:
> - `design/06-calendar/02-prototype/index.html` — clickable prototype (open in a browser)
> - `design/06-calendar/02-prototype/README.md` — what to try
> - `design/06-calendar/03-fixtures/calendar-fixture.json` — canonical demo dataset

---

## 0. TL;DR — the decision

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Where does the data live? | `<codx_path>/calendar/` — JSON documents written atomically, same conventions as `orchestration/runs/*.json`. **Not** inside the chat/board documents. |
| How many calendars? | Unlimited per project, like Google. Each has a colour, timezone, default reminders and ACL. |
| How does a task appear in several calendars? | The **item** owns the list of calendars (`calendar_ids[]`), not the calendar. A task is *always* in the system calendar `codx-junior` and *optionally* pinned to N user calendars. |
| What is the `codx-junior` calendar? | A **virtual, read-only system calendar** whose items are projections of task data (`Chat.due_date` / new `scheduled_start`/`scheduled_end`). It cannot hold hand-made events; it is computed on read. |
| Who expands recurrences and timezones? | The **server** returns *occurrences*, not events (precedent: `planning_manager.py` already derives flags/counts server-side). The client only renders. |
| How do reminders fire? | A background thread in `background.py` ticks every 30 s, dedupes through a persisted `delivered.json`, and emits a socket event. The client turns it into a toast + entry in the notification centre. |
| Google Calendar? | Phased: **ICS export/import** first, **read-only Google import** second, **two-way sync** last (highest risk, see §10). |
| Effort | ~4 milestones, §16. M0 (read + tasks + reminders) is the useful 60 %. |

---

## 1. Request, restated as requirements

| id | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| R1 | Visualise events and planning in an agenda (day / week / month / agenda list). |
| R2 | Create **multiple calendars** with own colour/visibility (Google Calendar behaviour). |
| R3 | **Notifications section** (a centre, not just a transient toast). |
| R4 | **Popup reminders** before an event starts. |
| R5 | A **`codx-junior` calendar** showing scheduled tasks, meets and orchestration runs. |
| R6 | A **task can belong to several calendars**. |
| R7 | Create, edit, move, resize, delete events; all-day and multi-day events. |
| R8 | Recurring events. |
| R9 | Guests/attendees on an event (at minimum a link to a project user). |
| R10 | Follow Google Calendar interaction conventions so no training is needed. |
| R11 | Must not break the existing Task Manager, Planning view or Meet scheduling. |
| R12 | Deep analysis + prototype **before** any change (this document + prototype). |

---

## 2. What already exists (evidence)

Everything below was read in the current tree. This is what we reuse versus what
we must build.

### 2.1 Reusable

| Piece | File | How the calendar uses it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Task fields | `api/codx/junior/db.py` → `Chat` | `due_date`, `priority`, `status`, `assignees`, `sprints`, `run_id`, `run_status`. Persisted through the existing `/api/chats/metadata` endpoint (it `setattr`s declared fields), so **new fields need no migration**. |
| Server-side derivation | `api/codx/junior/planning_manager.py` | Already computes `overdue / due_today / days_until_due` and server-side sorting. The calendar's occurrence expansion follows the same "server derives, client renders" rule. |
| File storage | `api/codx/junior/orchestration/store.py` | The exact pattern to copy: one JSON document per entity, `NamedTemporaryFile` + `fsync` + `os.replace`, `flock` for cross-process exclusion. |
| Router registration | `api/codx/junior/api/__init__.py` → `discover_routers()` | Any new `api/calendar.py` exporting `router` is mounted automatically at `/api`. No `app.py` edit needed. |
| Background loops | `api/codx/junior/background.py` → `start_background_services()` | Where the reminder ticker is added (a daemon thread next to `check_projects`). |
| Socket broadcast | `api/codx/junior/sio/session_channel.py`, `events/event_manager.py` | `EventManager.send_notification(**kwargs)` and `channel.send_event(name, payload)` (no `sid` = broadcast). |
| Cross-client invalidation | `api/codx/junior/events/collection_events.py` | Add `calendars` / `calendar_events` to `COLLECTIONS` so every open tab reloads. |
| Notification store | `client/src/store/ui.js` → `notifications[]`, `addNotification` | The existing 30 s auto-expiring toast list. R4 needs a **persistent** centre next to it, not a replacement. |
| Notification UI | `client/src/components/Notifications.vue`, `NotificationControl.vue`, `EventBar.vue` | The bell already exists in the top bar and already merges "recent events" + typed notifications. Extend it with a calendar section instead of inventing a second bell. |
| App/route registry | `client/src/config/apps.js`, `appComponentsMap.js`, `router/index.ts` | One registry entry + one route + one lazy component = the screen is reachable from the sidebar, dockview and mobile. |
| API modules | `client/src/api/api.js` + `client/src/api/modules/*.js` | `calendarModule(API)` registered with the lazy `API._calendarModule` getter. |
| Vuex modules | `client/src/store/index.js` | `import * as calendar from './calendar'` and it is `init()`-ed automatically. |
| Meets | `api/codx/junior/meets/*`, `api/codx/junior/api/meets.py` | A meet is a *live* room; the calendar shows future/held meets as items with `refs.meet_id`. **`MeetManager` is in-memory only** — calendar events must therefore be the durable record of a scheduled meet. |
| Orchestration runs | `api/codx/junior/orchestration/*` | `run_id`, `run_status`, `created_at` give the "scheduled work" items for the `codx-junior` calendar. |
| Design tokens | `design/tokens/design-tokens.json` | Colours for calendars (brand magenta + the existing `chartSeries` palette). |

### 2.2 Gaps — what does not exist

| Gap | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| No calendar storage | Nothing under `.codx/` holds events. `client/src/components/solopreneur/SolopreneurCalendar.vue` is a **static mock** (`useSolopreneur.js` state, grouped list, no dates). |
| `due_date` is a *date*, not a slot | `Chat.due_date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`. There is no start/end datetime, no duration, no all-day flag → a task cannot be laid out on an hour grid. |
| One calendar per task, implicitly | Tasks have `sprints[]` and `board/column`, but no `calendar_ids[]`. |
| No recurrence engine | No RRULE anywhere; `python-dateutil` is **not** in `api/pyproject.toml` dependencies (verified) and the client only has `moment` (no `moment-timezone`, no `rrule`). |
| No reminder scheduler | Nothing computes "notify N minutes before X". `EventManager.send_notification` is push-only, with no scheduling or dedupe. |
| Notifications are ephemeral | `ui.addNotification` removes the entry after 30 s and keeps it in memory only → a missed reminder is lost forever. |
| No notification centre | `Notifications.vue` shows the last 3 items of a rolling list; there is no unread state, no "mark as read", no persistence. |
| No ICS / Google layer | Nothing. The only OAuth implementation is GitHub (`security/github_oauth.py`). |
| Meet has no schedule | `Meet` has `created_at`/`ended_at` only; a "meet at 15:00 tomorrow" cannot be represented. |

---

## 3. Domain model

Four entities. `Calendar` and `CalendarEvent` are stored; `Occurrence` and
`Reminder` are derived.

```mermaid
erDiagram
    CALENDAR ||--o{ EVENT_CALENDAR : "lists"
    EVENT ||--o{ EVENT_CALENDAR : "appears in"
    EVENT ||--o{ REMINDER : "schedules"
    EVENT ||--o{ OCCURRENCE : "expands to"
    CHAT ||--o{ OCCURRENCE : "projects into (source=task)"
    MEET ||--o{ OCCURRENCE : "projects into (source=meet)"

    CALENDAR {
        string id PK
        string name
        string color
        string kind "personal|team|project|system|external"
        string timezone
        bool read_only
        json default_reminders
        json members
        bool visible
    }
    EVENT {
        string id PK
        string title
        string start "UTC ISO"
        string end "UTC ISO"
        bool all_day
        json recurrence "RRULE + exdates + overrides"
        json reminders
        string source "native|task|meet|orchestration|external"
        json refs "chat_id|meet_id|run_id"
        int revision
    }
    EVENT_CALENDAR {
        string event_id FK
        string calendar_id FK
    }
    OCCURRENCE {
        string event_id FK
        string calendar_ids
        string start
        string end
        string original_start "recurring only"
        bool is_recurring_instance
    }
```

### 3.1 Calendar

```json
{
  "id": "cal_work",
  "name": "Work",
  "color": "#CC0099",
  "description": "",
  "kind": "personal",
  "timezone": "Europe/Madrid",
  "read_only": false,
  "provider": "local",
  "default_reminders": [{ "channel": "popup", "minutes_before": 10 }],
  "members": [{ "user": "alice", "role": "owner" }],
  "visible": true,
  "order": 0,
  "created_at": "2026-02-01T09:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-02-01T09:00:00Z"
}
```

`kind` drives behaviour:

| kind | writable | Origin | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `personal` | yes | created by a user | "Work", "Personal" |
| `team` | yes (members) | one per project team | "Team — Platform" |
| `project` | yes | one per project, auto-created | "acme — delivery" |
| `system` | **no** | generated | `codx-junior` (tasks/meets/runs) |
| `external` | no | imported | "Holidays (ICS)", Google calendars |

### 3.2 CalendarEvent

```json
{
  "id": "evt_01JQ8Z…",
  "calendar_ids": ["cal_work", "cal_personal"],
  "title": "Spec review — calendar manager",
  "description": "Walk through §4 storage + §7 reminders.",
  "location": "Meet /meet/9f2a",
  "start": "2026-02-10T09:00:00Z",
  "end": "2026-02-10T10:00:00Z",
  "all_day": false,
  "timezone": "Europe/Madrid",
  "recurrence": null,
  "reminders": [
    { "channel": "popup", "minutes_before": 15 },
    { "channel": "popup", "minutes_before": 0 }
  ],
  "status": "confirmed",
  "visibility": "default",
  "source": "native",
  "refs": {},
  "guests": ["marta"],
  "created_by": "alice",
  "created_at": "2026-02-03T10:12:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-02-03T10:12:00Z",
  "revision": 1
}
```

**Invariants**

1. `calendar_ids` is non-empty, deduplicated, and every id must resolve to an
   existing calendar (validated on write; a dangling id is returned by
   `GET /calendars?orphans=1` for repair, never silently dropped).
2. A `system` or `external` calendar can never appear alone in
   `calendar_ids` in a *write*: content coming from a projection cannot be
   edited (409 `read_only_calendar`).
3. `end > start` unless `all_day` (then `end = start + 1 day` inclusive-exclusive).
4. `revision` is incremented on every write; clients send `If-Match` (§5.3).
5. A recurring event stores the **first** `start`; instances are computed.
6. A recurring event **cannot span calendars differently per instance** (a
   Google limitation we intentionally keep: it removes a whole class of bugs).

### 3.3 Occurrence (derived, never stored)

```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_01JQ8Z…",
  "calendar_ids": ["cal_work", "cal_personal"],
  "title": "Spec review — calendar manager",
  "start": "2026-02-10T09:00:00Z",
  "end": "2026-02-10T10:00:00Z",
  "all_day": false,
  "source": "native",
  "refs": {},
  "calendar_id": "cal_work",
  "is_recurring_instance": false,
  "original_start": null,
  "overdue": false,
  "read_only": false
}
```

`calendar_id` (singular) is the calendar whose colour the chip uses; the full
`calendar_ids` list is what the UI shows as multi-calendar badges. This is the
key to R6: **one occurrence, N memberships.**

### 3.4 Reminder (derived)

```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_01JQ8Z…",
  "occurrence_start": "2026-02-10T09:00:00Z",
  "minutes_before": 15,
  "channel": "popup",
  "trigger_at": "2026-02-10T08:45:00Z",
  "delivered_at": null
}
```

---

## 4. Storage design

### 4.1 Layout

```
<codx_path>/calendar/
├── calendars.json                 # [Calendar]  — small, single document
├── events/
│   ├── 2026-01.json               # [CalendarEvent] keyed by start month (UTC)
│   ├── 2026-02.json
│   └── 2026-03.json
├── delivered.json                 # reminder dedupe (see §7.3)
├── settings.json                  # window prefs, default calendar, week start
└── export/
    └── cal_work.ics               # generated feed (git-ignored)
```

### 4.2 Why not store this on the Chat / board document?

- A board document is rewritten wholesale on every card move; adding events
  there would multiply write amplification and lock contention.
- Events are **not** tasks: they have guests, recurrence and reminders, and they
  must be queryable by date range across the whole project.
- Tasks only ever *project* into the calendar. Keeping the projection read-only
  guarantees that the Task Manager stays the single writer of task data.

### 4.3 Conventions copied from `orchestration/store.py`

- **Atomic write**: temp file in the same directory → `flush` → `fsync` →
  `os.replace`. A crash can never leave half a month file.
- **Cross-process exclusion**: `fcntl.flock` on `calendar/.lock` while a write is
  in flight (the API runs several uvicorn workers — see the comment in
  `pyproject.toml` about multi-worker deployments, the same hazard applies here).
- **Bounded, validated ids**: `os.path.basename()` on every id before building a
  path, exactly like `RunStore.run_path`.
- **Tolerant reads**: a corrupt month file is logged and skipped; the calendar
  still renders (never a 500 because of one bad file).

### 4.4 Month sharding and the overlap problem

Query windows are small by nature (month view = 3 shards, week = 2, agenda = 2).
A long event (holiday, offsite) may start before the window and overlap into it.
Rule:

> An event is stored in the shard of its **start** month, and a range query reads
> `[from - MAX_EVENT_DURATION, to]` where `MAX_EVENT_DURATION = 31 days`.
> Events longer than 31 days are rejected on write (400 `event_too_long`); a
> "long" period must be a recurring event or an all-day per-day block.

This keeps every query at ≤ 4 file reads with no index to maintain. If a project
ever exceeds ~20 k events, add `events/index.json` (`{id, month, start, end,
calendar_ids}`) — that is the documented escape hatch, not part of M0.

### 4.5 Size budget

| Item | Estimate |
| --- | --- |
| Calendar | ~400 B |
| Event (with description) | ~1 KB |
| 2 000 events / year / project | ≈ 2 MB total, ≈ 170 KB per shard |

Comfortably JSON. No database, no migration of existing data.

---

## 5. Backend API (contract)

All routes live in a new `api/codx/junior/api/calendar.py` exporting `router`
(auto-discovered, mounted at `/api`). Project scope comes from
`request.state.codx_junior_session.settings`, like `meets.py` and `management.py`.

### 5.1 Calendars

| Method | Path | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/calendar/calendars` | Includes materialised `system` + `external` entries. |
| `POST` | `/api/calendar/calendars` | `{name, color, kind?, timezone?, default_reminders?}` → 201. |
| `PUT` | `/api/calendar/calendars/{id}` | Partial update (name, color, visible, order, reminders). |
| `DELETE` | `/api/calendar/calendars/{id}?move_to={other}` | 409 if it still has events and `move_to` was not given. A `system` calendar returns 409 `read_only_calendar`. |

### 5.2 Events and occurrences

| Method | Path | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/api/calendar/events/query` | **The main read**: `{calendar_ids?, from, to, q?, sources?, include_hidden?}` → `{range, calendars, occurrences[], counts}`. Recurrences are expanded server-side. |
| `GET` | `/api/calendar/events/{id}` | Raw event (for the editor, which needs the rule, not the instances). |
| `POST` | `/api/calendar/events` | Create. `calendar_ids[]` required. |
| `PUT` | `/api/calendar/events/{id}` | Update. `If-Match: <revision>`; 409 `revision_mismatch` otherwise. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/calendar/events/{id}?scope=single\|following\|all` | Recurring delete semantics, same three options as Google. |
| `POST` | `/api/calendar/events/{id}/snooze` | `{minutes, occurrence_start}` → reschedules the reminder. |
| `POST` | `/api/calendar/events/quick` | `{text}` → parsed draft (`"Lunch Ana tom 13:00 1h @Café"`), **not persisted** until confirmed. |

Why a `POST /query` instead of `GET /events?from=…`: the request carries arrays
(calendar ids, sources) and grows; `POST` matches the existing
`POST /api/management/tasks/query` and `POST /api/planning/*` convention.

**Response sketch**

```json
{
  "range": { "from": "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z", "to": "2026-03-01T00:00:00Z", "timezone": "Europe/Madrid" },
  "calendars": [{ "id": "cal_work", "name": "Work", "color": "#CC0099", "read_only": false }],
  "occurrences": [ /* §3.3 */ ],
  "counts": { "by_calendar": { "cal_work": 12 }, "by_source": { "task": 5, "native": 7 } }
}
```

### 5.3 Concurrency, errors and events

- Optimistic locking with `revision` + `If-Match`. Two tabs editing the same
  event: the loser gets `409 revision_mismatch` with the current document so the
  UI can show a diff, instead of silently overwriting.
- Error codes (string `detail` prefix, consistent with `HTTPException` usage
  across the API): `read_only_calendar`, `revision_mismatch`, `event_too_long`,
  `invalid_recurrence`, `unknown_calendar`, `calendar_in_use`.
- After every successful write:
  `emit_collection_event(COLLECTION_CALENDAR_EVENTS, action, {id, calendar_ids}, settings=…)`
  → every open tab reloads only the affected range (new entries added to
  `COLLECTIONS` in `collection_events.py`).

### 5.4 Task → calendar fields

Extend `Chat` (`api/codx/junior/db.py`). All have defaults, so old task files load
unchanged and the existing `POST /api/chats/metadata` path persists them with no
new endpoint:

```python
calendar_ids: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list,
    description="Calendars this task is pinned to, beyond the implicit 'codx-junior' one")
scheduled_start: Optional[str] = None   # ISO datetime, the time block
scheduled_end:   Optional[str] = None   # ISO datetime
all_day: bool = False
```

`due_date` stays a **date** and keeps its meaning (deadline) — the calendar draws
it as an all-day marker with a deadline flag, while `scheduled_start/end` is the
work block. Conflating them would break the overdue logic in
`planning_manager.py`, which is tested and consumed by the Planning view.

---

## 6. The `codx-junior` calendar (R5 + R6)

A virtual calendar, present in every project, **read-only**. Its items are
projected from data we already own:

| Source | Rule | Badge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Task with `scheduled_start/end` | Block at that time. | `Task` |
| Task with `due_date`, no schedule | All-day marker on the due date; `overdue` styling if `due < today` and `status != done`. | `Due` |
| Orchestration run (`run_id`, `run_status`) | Block from `started_at`, or all-day if not started. | `Run` |
| Meet | Block at the scheduled time (needs the new `Meet.scheduled_start`, §11). | `Meet` |

Properties:

- **Not writable.** Dragging a `codx-junior` item moves the *task* (calls
  `PUT /api/planning/tasks/{id}`-equivalent), not an event. This is the behaviour
  that makes the calendar useful instead of a second task board.
- **Filterable** by source, board, sprint, assignee, status
  (the query's `sources` + `boards` fields), reusing the planning filters.
- **Multi-calendar**: a task shows *simultaneously* in `codx-junior` and in any
  calendar in its `calendar_ids`. Adding it to "Work" does not duplicate it; it
  is one task with two memberships, so completing it clears both.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    T[Chat / task<br/>scheduled_start, due_date, calendar_ids=['cal_work']]
    T --> P[Projection]
    P --> SYS[codx-junior calendar<br/>system, read-only]
    P --> W[Work calendar<br/>via calendar_ids]
    W -->|drag / resize| API[PUT /api/planning/tasks/:id]
    SYS -->|drag / resize| API
```

---

## 7. Notifications and popup reminders (R3 + R4)

### 7.1 Pipeline

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant BG as Background thread (30 s)
    participant ST as calendar store
    participant SIO as Socket.IO (broadcast)
    participant CL as Client store/calendar.js
    participant UI as NotificationCentre + popup

    BG->>ST: load events in [now-1d, now+7d]
    BG->>BG: expand occurrences, compute trigger_at = start - minutes
    BG->>ST: read delivered.json
    BG->>BG: due = trigger_at <= now and not delivered
    BG->>ST: append to delivered.json (atomic)
    BG->>SIO: emit codx-junior-calendar-reminder {occurrence, minutes_before}
    SIO->>CL: event
    CL->>UI: push notification + show popup card
    UI->>ST: POST /events/{id}/snooze  (optional)
```

### 7.2 Why a background thread and not "the browser sets a timeout"

The browser timer is the easy path and it is wrong: it dies with the tab, it
cannot deliver when the app is closed, and a laptop asleep at 09:45 never fires
the 10:00 reminder. The server tick also makes email/Web-Push a later plug-in
instead of a rewrite.

It still degrades gracefully: if the tick runs while nobody is connected, the
reminder is **marked delivered and persisted**, so the notification centre shows
it as "missed" the next time the client loads (`GET /api/calendar/reminders?since=`).

### 7.3 Delivery dedupe

`delivered.json`:

```json
{ "evt_01JQ8Z…|2026-02-10T09:00:00Z|15": "2026-02-10T08:45:03Z" }
```

Key = `event_id|occurrence_start|minutes_before`. Bounded: entries older than 30
days are pruned on every tick (≈ 3 events/day → a few hundred lines). Exactly the
same trick as the harness `notification_sent` flag (see
`api/tests/harness/test_harness_notification.py`: "must be sent exactly once …
the durable flag survives duplicate ticks/restarts").

### 7.4 Client side

- `store/calendar.js` (new Vuex module) holds `calendars`, `occurrences`,
  `notifications[]` (**persistent**, unlike `ui.notifications`), `unreadCount`.
- Socket handler registered once at `init()`:
  `API.socket.on('codx-junior-calendar-reminder', …)` (the `SocketManager.on`
  keeps named listeners across reconnects — verified in `api/socket.js`).
- `components/calendar/ReminderPopup.vue` — bottom-right card: title, time,
  "Snooze 5 / 10 min", "Dismiss", "Open". Auto-dismiss after 60 s **without**
  losing the notification-centre entry.
- `components/Notifications.vue` gains a third section ("Reminders") plus
  unread/read state. The transient `ui.addNotification` toasts stay for
  operational messages (they are not a reminder channel).
- Browser `Notification` API: **opt-in** toggle in the calendar settings, used
  only when the tab is backgrounded. Requires HTTPS/localhost.
- M3 extension: Web Push (service worker + VAPID) and email; both plug into the
  same tick, which is why the design keeps delivery out of the request path.

---

## 8. Recurrence and timezones

### 8.1 Model

Store **RFC 5545 RRULE** as a string, plus exceptions — the same shape Google
Calendar and ICS use, so export is lossless:

```json
"recurrence": {
  "rrule": "FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=1;BYDAY=MO,WE;UNTIL=20260630T000000Z",
  "exdates": ["2026-03-04T09:00:00Z"],
  "overrides": {
    "2026-03-11T09:00:00Z": { "start": "2026-03-11T14:00:00Z", "end": "2026-03-11T15:00:00Z", "title": "Spec review (moved)" }
  }
}
```

`overrides` keys are the *original* occurrence starts, i.e. `RECURRENCE-ID` in
ICS terms — a straight mapping.

### 8.2 Expansion rules (server)

- Expand only inside the requested range, hard-capped at
  `MAX_OCCURRENCES = 750` per event and a 2-year horizon (`invalid_recurrence`
  beyond that).
- Everything is computed in the **event's** timezone, then serialised as UTC.
  This is what makes `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO` stay at 09:00 local across a DST
  change instead of drifting to 08:00/10:00 as a naive UTC expansion does.
- `UNTIL` is inclusive; `COUNT` counts generated instances.

### 8.3 Dependencies (verified)

| Need | Today | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RRULE parsing/expansion (Python) | `python-dateutil` is **not** a declared dependency in `api/pyproject.toml` | Add `python-dateutil>=2.9` (pure-python, MIT, tiny). It ships `dateutil.rrule`, the reference implementation. |
| ICS import/export | not present | Add `icalendar>=6.0` (pure python). Alternatively hand-write the (small) VEVENT/VTIMEZONE subset — decide in M2. |
| Client recurrence | `moment` only (no `moment-timezone`, no `rrule`) | Not needed: the server returns occurrences. |
| Client timezone display | `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in the browser | Use it; no new client dependency. |

> Rule of thumb for this feature: **the browser never does date maths**. It
> formats what the API gives it. That is how the prototype is built too.

---

## 9. UI/UX

### 9.1 Screen anatomy (follows Google Calendar)

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Today  ‹ ›   February 2026            Month Week Day Agenda   🔔3  + Create │
├───────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ + Create      │  Mon  Tue  Wed  Thu  Fri  Sat  Sun                    │
│ mini month    │  ┌────┬────┬────┬────┬────┬────┬────┐                 │
│               │  │    │    │    │    │    │    │    │                 │
│ My calendars  │  └────┴────┴────┴────┴────┴────┴────┘                 │
│ ☑ Work        │                                                       │
│ ☑ Personal    │   Day cell: up to 3 chips + "+2 more"                 │
│ ☑ Team        │   Chip = calendar colour + optional 2nd colour dot    │
│ ☑ codx-junior │   for multi-calendar membership                        │
│ Other         │                                                       │
│ ☑ Holidays    │                                                       │
└───────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 9.2 Views

| View | Content | Key interaction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Month** | 6×7 grid, up to 3 chips per day, "+N more" opens the day | click day → create; click chip → detail popover |
| **Week** | 7 columns × 24 h, all-day row on top, overlaps side by side, "now" line | click/drag empty slot → create with prefilled time; drag event → move (optimistic + `PUT`) |
| **Day** | same as week, one column, 15-min slots | resize bottom edge → new `end` |
| **Agenda** | scrollable list grouped by day, 30 days from the cursor, with filters | infinite scroll (reuse the planning pattern: `PAGE_SIZE` + `loadNextPage`) |
| **Sidebar mini** | 6-week mini month, dots per day, click → jump | — |

### 9.3 Interaction rules that matter

1. **Colour = calendar.** A chip's bar uses the primary calendar colour; when the
   item belongs to more than one calendar, the bar becomes a two-tone gradient
   and the tooltip lists them. This is how R6 stays visible without clutter.
2. **Source badge, not colour, marks provenance.** `Task`, `Due`, `Run`, `Meet`
   are small textual badges. Provenance is orthogonal to membership.
3. **Read-only items are visibly different**: no resize handles, an info line
   "Managed by the Task Manager → *open task*".
4. **Optimistic updates.** Move/resize renders instantly and reconciles with the
   server response; on `409 revision_mismatch` the item snaps back with a toast.
5. **Keyboard**: `n` new, `t` today, `m/w/d/a` views, `←/→` navigate, `/` search,
   `Esc` close, `Delete` on a focused chip.
6. **Empty/loading/error**: skeleton grid while the first query resolves; a
   calendar with zero occurrences keeps its colour in the sidebar but draws no
   chips; a shard read error shows a per-day inline warning instead of a blank
   screen.
7. **Mobile**: the month grid becomes the default; day/agenda replace week; the
   sidebar becomes a drawer; "swipe to navigate periods" (the route already has
   `meta.mobile` conventions to follow).

### 9.4 Where the screen lives

Registry work (three lines + one component), following `config/apps.js`:

```js
// config/apps.js
calendar: {
  id: 'calendar', title: 'Calendar', component: 'calendar', icon: 'fa-regular fa-calendar-days',
  route: () => ({ name: 'calendar' })
}
```
```js
// config/appComponentsMap.js
'calendar': lazy(() => import('../views/CalendarView.vue'))
```
```ts
// router/index.ts
{ path: '/:projectName/calendar', name: 'calendar', component: AppRouteView,
  meta: { app: 'calendar', ...mobile('Calendar', 'more') } }
```

That single registration makes it a dockview panel on desktop and a route on
mobile — no branching code.

---

## 10. Google Calendar / ICS interoperability

The request says "we can follow Google Calendar". Chasing two-way sync in M0
would sink the milestone (the Google Calendar API has incremental sync tokens,
per-instance recurrence overrides, ACLs, `watch` channels that must be renewed,
quota units per project, and it *rejects* some RRULEs we may want to allow).
Recommended ladder:

| Step | Scope | Effort | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **M2a — ICS export** | `GET /api/calendar/feed/{calendar_id}.ics?token=…` per calendar, plus one "all calendars" feed. Token = HMAC of `calendar_id + user`, no OAuth needed. Add-to-Google/Apple works immediately. | S | Low |
| **M2b — ICS import** | Upload a `.ics`, preview the diff, then import into a chosen calendar. Read-only re-import by `UID` for idempotency. | M | Low |
| **M3 — Google read-only** | OAuth (reuse the PKCE flow pattern of `security/github_oauth.py`), import calendars as `kind: "external"`, refresh with `syncToken`, one-way Google → codx-junior. | M/L | Medium |
| **M4 — two-way** | Push local writes, resolve conflicts (last-writer-wins + a conflict notification), instance-level overrides, Meet link import, watch channels. | L | **High** |

Explicit non-goals for v1: Google **Meet** creation from the event editor,
Gmail invitations, shared-calendar ACL mirroring, free/busy across accounts.

---

## 11. Multi-user, permissions, and one Meet gap

- **Calendars** carry `members[{user, role}]` with `owner|writer|reader`.
  Resolution reuses the project ACL already enforced by `get_authenticated_user`
  and the profile/project permission helpers.
- **Events** inherit the ACL of their calendars; `visibility: private` restricts
  the body to the creator and hides the title ("Private") from other members.
- `system`/`external` calendars are `read_only` for everyone.
- **Meet gap (must fix in M1)**: `Meet` (`api/codx/junior/meets/model.py`) has no
  `scheduled_start`. To show a *future* meet on the calendar we add
  `scheduled_start`, `scheduled_end`, `calendar_ids` to `Meet`, and a
  `POST /api/meets/schedule` that creates the meet **and** its calendar event in
  one transaction. Note that `MeetManager` keeps meets in memory only
  (`self._meets` dict), so today a meet literally disappears on restart — the
  calendar event becomes the durable record and fixes an existing weakness for
  free.

---

## 12. Performance budgets

| Scenario | Budget |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /events/query` month view (3 shards, 3 calendars, ~500 occurrences) | < 60 ms p95 |
| Same, with 20 recurring events × 750 instances | < 150 ms (cap `MAX_OCCURRENCES`, paginate agenda) |
| Client render month grid | < 16 ms/frame, no re-render on hover (chips are CSS-only) |
| Reminder tick per project | < 20 ms; ≤ 7 days of events loaded |
| Socket payload for a reminder | < 2 KB |

Guard rails: the query rejects ranges wider than 92 days (the agenda paginates);
recurrence expansion is capped; `delivered.json` is pruned.

---

## 13. Accessibility

- Grid is a real table-semantics structure (`role="grid"`, `aria-rowcount`,
  cells focusable, arrow-key navigation between days).
- Chips are `<button>` with `aria-label="Spec review, 10:00–11:00, Work"`.
- Colour is never the only signal: every chip also carries its calendar's initial
  or a dot pattern, so the magenta/green pair is distinguishable for
  deuteranopia (the brand palette's magenta↔green pair is a known risky pair —
  verified in `design/tokens/design-tokens.json` `chartSeries`).
- Reminder popup: `role="alert"`, focusable actions, no auto-dismiss when
  `prefers-reduced-motion` + keyboard focus is inside.
- Minimum hit target 32 px in the month grid; 44 px on mobile.

---

## 14. Test strategy

| Level | What |
| --- | --- |
| Unit (Python) | Store round-trip; atomic write under a simulated crash; month-shard boundary; recurrence expansion incl. DST boundary and `COUNT`/`UNTIL`; reminder dedupe across two ticks and a restart. |
| Unit (JS) | Occurrence layout (overlap lanes), chip density ("+N more"), view range maths. |
| API | Query contract with the fixture; `revision_mismatch`; `read_only_calendar`; ACL for a `reader`. |
| Integration | Task with `calendar_ids` shows in two calendars and in `codx-junior`; editing it in the calendar goes through the planning endpoint. |
| E2E (browser profile) | Create a calendar → create an event with a reminder → advance the server clock → assert the popup and the notification centre. |
| Prototype | `02-prototype/index.html` is the visual acceptance artefact for the UX review. |

Fixtures: `03-fixtures/calendar-fixture.json` (also used to seed a demo project).

---

## 15. Risks

| # | Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Task projection drifts from the Task Manager | Users see two truths | One single projection function, server-side; the calendar **never** writes task fields except through the planning API. |
| 2 | `due_date` vs `scheduled_*` confusion | Wrong priority/overdue logic | Keep both, document them, draw `due` as an all-day deadline marker (§6). |
| 3 | Reminder duplicates / losses | Trust damage | Persisted dedupe key + restart test; 30 s tick with a `now-1d` look-back window. |
| 4 | Timezone/DST bugs in recurrence | Meetings one hour off | Compute in the event timezone, store UTC, test the DST weekend explicitly. |
| 5 | Unbounded recurrence expansion | Latency spike | `MAX_OCCURRENCES`, 92-day query cap, 2-year horizon. |
| 6 | Multi-calendar writes to Google (later) | Sync loops | Local `calendar_ids` are ours; a Google event is imported into **one** external calendar only. |
| 7 | Notification fatigue | Users mute everything | Per-calendar reminder defaults, max 2 reminders per event, quiet hours in `settings.json`. |
| 8 | Board/planning regressions | Broken Task Manager | New `Chat` fields are additive with defaults; the planning tests must stay green before merging. |
| 9 | The existing `SolopreneurCalendar.vue` mock confuses readers | Wrong screen maintained | It is deleted/pointed at the real store in M1 (it is mock-only, verified). |

---

## 16. Delivery plan

| Milestone | Content | Acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **M0 — foundations** (≈ 3–4 days) | `calendar/` store + models, `api/calendar.py` (calendars + query + events CRUD), `store/calendar.js`, `views/CalendarView.vue` with month/week/agenda, sidebar with **multiple calendars**. `Chat.calendar_ids/scheduled_*`. | Create 2 calendars, put a task in both, see it in month/week. Fixture-driven test green. |
| **M1 — codx-junior + writes** (≈ 3–4 days) | System-calendar projection (task/run/meet), drag & resize writing back through the planning API, `Meet.scheduled_*` + schedule endpoint, editor modal with guests. | Dragging a task chip reschedules the task; a scheduled meet appears and survives restart. |
| **M2 — reminders** (≈ 3 days) | Background ticker, `delivered.json`, socket event, notification centre (unread/read/missed), `ReminderPopup.vue`, snooze, opt-in browser notifications. | Reminder fires exactly once, survives a restart, appears in the centre after being missed. |
| **M3 — recurrence + interop** (≈ 4 days) | RRULE + overrides, per-instance edit/delete, ICS export, ICS import. | A weekly event keeps 09:00 across the DST change; the `.ics` opens in Google Calendar. |
| **M4 — Google two-way** (≈ 5–8 days) | OAuth, incremental sync, conflict handling, watch renewal. | Documented, and only after M0–M3 are in use. |

Sequence is deliberate: **M0 has no new dependency and no background work**, so
it can ship and be evaluated while the harder parts are designed.

---

## 17. Open questions (need a decision before M0 code)

1. **Scope of calendars** — per project only, or also installation-wide
   calendars visible in every project? (The prototype assumes per project + a
   global `codx-junior` projection.)
2. **Who owns `personal` calendars** — each user has private calendars, or is
   everything project-visible? This decides whether the store needs per-user
   partitioning.
3. **Meets** — is the calendar the place to *schedule* a meet (create it ahead of
   time), or only to display meets that already exist?
4. **Working hours / capacity** — do we want the calendar to feed a
   capacity/allocation model (per assignee) as Google's "working hours" does?
   This changes the projection: `assignees[]` would need per-day capacity.
5. **Email/push delivery** — is email a must for reminders, and is there already
   SMTP configuration in global settings to reuse?
6. **Google** — is *read* enough for the first release (import my Google
   calendars) or is *write* required to consider the feature done?

---

  .spacer{flex:1}
  .sim{
    display:flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;padding:4px 8px;border-radius:999px;
    border:1px dashed color-mix(in oklch,var(--warning) 45%,transparent);
    background:color-mix(in oklch,var(--warning) 8%,transparent); font-size:11px;
  }
  .sim b{font-family:var(--mono);font-weight:600;color:var(--warning)}
  .sim .btn{padding:3px 8px;font-size:11px}
  .bell{position:relative;width:34px;height:34px;border-radius:50%;display:grid;place-items:center;font-size:15px}
  .bell:hover{background:var(--overlay)}
  .bell .badge{
    position:absolute;top:0;right:0;min-width:16px;height:16px;border-radius:9px;padding:0 4px;
    background:var(--error);color:#fff;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;display:grid;place-items:center;
    border:2px solid var(--raised);
  }

  /* ── sidebar ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  aside{
    border-right:1px solid var(--border); background:var(--raised);
    overflow:auto; padding:12px; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:14px;
  }
  .create{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;border:1px solid var(--border-strong);
    background:var(--overlay);border-radius:999px;padding:9px 14px;font-weight:600;
    box-shadow:0 1px 0 color-mix(in oklch,var(--text) 6%,transparent)}
  .create:hover{background:color-mix(in oklch,var(--overlay) 80%, var(--primary) 12%)}
  .create .plus{width:18px;height:18px;display:grid;place-items:center;color:var(--primary);font-size:16px}

  .mini{user-select:none}
  .mini-head{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;margin-bottom:6px}
  .mini-title{font-size:12px;font-weight:600}
  .mini-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(7,1fr);gap:1px;text-align:center}
  .mini-grid .dow{font-size:10px;color:var(--faint);padding:2px 0}
  .mini-day{
    position:relative;padding:4px 0;border-radius:50%;font-size:11px;color:var(--muted);
    aspect-ratio:1;display:grid;place-items:center;
  }
  .mini-day:hover{background:var(--overlay);color:var(--text)}
  .mini-day.other{opacity:.35}
  .mini-day.today{background:var(--primary);color:var(--primary-ink);font-weight:700}
  .mini-day.cursor{outline:1.5px solid var(--primary);outline-offset:-1px}
  .mini-dots{position:absolute;bottom:1px;left:0;right:0;display:flex;gap:1px;justify-content:center}
  .mini-dots i{width:3px;height:3px;border-radius:50%;display:block}

  .section-title{font-size:10px;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--faint);font-weight:700;margin-bottom:2px}
  .cal-list{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:1px}
  .cal-row{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:9px;padding:6px 6px;border-radius:8px;text-align:left;width:100%}
  .cal-row:hover{background:var(--overlay)}
  .cal-check{
    width:14px;height:14px;border-radius:4px;border:1.5px solid var(--cc);
    display:grid;place-items:center;flex:0 0 auto;background:var(--cc);
  }
  .cal-check.off{background:transparent}
  .cal-check svg{opacity:0}
  .cal-check:not(.off) svg{opacity:1}
  .cal-name{flex:1;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis;white-space:nowrap}
  .cal-row .meta{font-size:10px;color:var(--faint);font-family:var(--mono)}
  .cal-row.readonly .cal-name{color:var(--muted)}
  .tag{font-size:9px;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.06em;padding:1px 5px;border-radius:4px;
    border:1px solid var(--border-strong);color:var(--faint)}
  .tag.ro{color:var(--warning);border-color:color-mix(in oklch,var(--warning) 40%,transparent)}
  .hint{font-size:11px;line-height:1.5;color:var(--faint);margin:0}
  details.help{border-top:1px solid var(--border);padding-top:10px}
  details.help summary{cursor:pointer;font-size:11px;color:var(--muted);font-weight:600}
  details.help ul{margin:8px 0 0 14px;padding:0;font-size:11px;line-height:1.6;color:var(--faint)}
  details.help kbd{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:10px;border:1px solid var(--border-strong);
    border-radius:4px;padding:0 4px;background:var(--sunken)}

  /* ── main ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  main{overflow:hidden;position:relative;display:flex;flex-direction:column;min-width:0}
  .week-head{display:grid;grid-template-columns:56px repeat(7,1fr);border-bottom:1px solid var(--border);
    background:var(--raised);flex:0 0 auto}
  .week-head .corner{border-right:1px solid var(--border)}
  .day-head{padding:6px 4px;text-align:center;border-right:1px solid var(--border)}
  .day-head .dow{font-size:10px;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.08em;color:var(--faint)}
  .day-head .num{font-size:17px;font-weight:600;line-height:1.2}
  .day-head.today .num{color:var(--primary)}
  .day-head .num{display:inline-grid;place-items:center;min-width:30px;height:30px;border-radius:50%;margin-top:2px}
  .day-head.today .num{background:var(--primary);color:var(--primary-ink)}
  .allday-row{display:grid;grid-template-columns:56px repeat(7,1fr);border-bottom:1px solid var(--border);
    background:var(--bg);flex:0 0 auto;max-height:92px;overflow:auto}
  .allday-row .label{font-size:10px;color:var(--faint);text-align:right;padding:4px 6px;border-right:1px solid var(--border)}
  .allday-cell{padding:2px 3px;border-right:1px solid var(--border);display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:2px;min-height:26px}

  .scroll{overflow:auto;flex:1;position:relative}
  .grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:56px repeat(7,1fr);position:relative}
  .hours{position:relative}
  .hour-lab{height:var(--hph);font-size:10px;color:var(--faint);text-align:right;padding-right:6px;
    transform:translateY(-6px);font-family:var(--mono)}
  .day-col{position:relative;border-right:1px solid var(--border);height:calc(24 * var(--hph))}
  .day-col .slot{position:absolute;left:0;right:0;height:var(--hph);border-top:1px solid
    color-mix(in oklch,var(--text) 7%,transparent)}
  .day-col .slot:hover{background:color-mix(in oklch,var(--text) 4%, transparent)}
  .day-col.weekend{background:color-mix(in oklch,var(--text) 2.5%, transparent)}
  .nowline{position:absolute;left:0;right:0;height:0;border-top:2px solid var(--error);z-index:5;pointer-events:none}
  .nowline::before{content:"";position:absolute;left:-5px;top:-5px;width:8px;height:8px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--error)}

  /* ── chips ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  .chip{
    position:relative;display:block;width:100%;text-align:left;border-radius:6px;
    padding:2px 6px 2px 7px;font-size:11px;line-height:1.35;overflow:hidden;
    background:color-mix(in oklch, var(--cc) 22%, var(--raised));
    border-left:3px solid var(--cc); cursor:pointer;
  }
  .chip:hover{background:color-mix(in oklch, var(--cc) 34%, var(--raised))}
  .chip.multi{border-left-color:transparent;
    background-image:linear-gradient(to right, var(--cc) 0 3px, var(--cc2) 3px 6px, transparent 6px),
      linear-gradient(color-mix(in oklch,var(--cc) 20%, var(--raised)), color-mix(in oklch,var(--cc2) 20%, var(--raised)));
    background-size:6px 100%, 100% 100%; background-repeat:no-repeat;
    padding-left:10px;}
  .chip.timed{border-left-width:3px;padding:2px 5px 2px 6px;border-radius:5px}
  .chip .t{color:var(--muted);font-size:10px;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
  .chip .badges{display:inline-flex;gap:3px;margin-left:4px;vertical-align:baseline}
  .badge-src{font-size:8px;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.05em;padding:0 3px;border-radius:3px;
    background:color-mix(in oklch,var(--text) 14%,transparent);color:var(--text);font-weight:700}
  .badge-src.due{background:color-mix(in oklch,var(--warning) 30%,transparent);color:var(--warning)}
  .badge-src.overdue{background:color-mix(in oklch,var(--error) 30%,transparent);color:var(--error)}
  .chip.past{opacity:.55}
  .chip .dots{display:inline-flex;gap:2px;margin-left:4px}
  .chip .dots i{width:5px;height:5px;border-radius:50%;display:block}
  .block{
    position:absolute;left:2px;border-radius:6px;padding:2px 5px;overflow:hidden;font-size:11px;
    line-height:1.3;border-left:3px solid var(--cc);
    background:color-mix(in oklch, var(--cc) 26%, var(--raised));
    box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.35); cursor:pointer;
  }
  .block:hover{background:color-mix(in oklch, var(--cc) 38%, var(--raised));z-index:6}
  .block .ttl{font-weight:600;white-space:nowrap;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis}
  .block .t{font-size:10px;color:var(--muted);font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
  .block .resize{position:absolute;left:0;right:0;bottom:0;height:6px;cursor:ns-resize}

  /* ── month ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  .month{display:flex;flex-direction:column;flex:1;overflow:hidden}
  .month-head{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(7,1fr);border-bottom:1px solid var(--border);
    background:var(--raised);flex:0 0 auto}
  .month-head div{padding:6px;text-align:center;font-size:10px;letter-spacing:.08em;
    text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--faint);border-right:1px solid var(--border)}
  .month-body{flex:1;display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(7,1fr);grid-template-rows:repeat(6,1fr);
    overflow:auto}
  .mcell{border-right:1px solid var(--border);border-bottom:1px solid var(--border);padding:3px 4px;
    display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:2px;min-height:0;overflow:hidden;position:relative}
  .mcell.other{background:color-mix(in oklch,var(--text) 2%, transparent)}
  .mcell.today{background:color-mix(in oklch,var(--primary) 8%, transparent)}
  .mcell .num{font-size:11px;color:var(--muted);text-align:center;width:20px;height:20px;
    display:grid;place-items:center;border-radius:50%;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
  .mcell.today .num{background:var(--primary);color:var(--primary-ink);font-weight:700}
  .mcell .more{font-size:10px;color:var(--muted);padding-left:6px;text-align:left}
  .mcell .more:hover{color:var(--text)}
  .mcell .clickzone{position:absolute;inset:0;z-index:0}

  /* ── agenda ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  .agenda{overflow:auto;padding:8px 16px 60px;flex:1}
  .ag-day{margin-top:14px}
  .ag-day h4{position:sticky;top:0;background:var(--bg);margin:0;padding:6px 0;font-size:11px;
    text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.08em;color:var(--faint);z-index:2;
    display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center}
  .ag-day h4 .line{flex:1;height:1px;background:var(--border)}
  .ag-day.today h4{color:var(--primary)}
  .ag-row{display:flex;gap:12px;align-items:flex-start;padding:8px 10px;border-radius:10px;
    border:1px solid transparent;cursor:pointer}
  .ag-row:hover{background:var(--raised);border-color:var(--border)}
  .ag-time{width:96px;flex:0 0 auto;font-family:var(--mono);font-size:11px;color:var(--muted);padding-top:2px}
  .ag-main{flex:1;min-width:0}
  .ag-title{font-weight:600;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;flex-wrap:wrap}
  .ag-sub{font-size:11px;color:var(--faint);margin-top:2px;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis;white-space:nowrap}
  .ag-cal{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:5px;font-size:10px;color:var(--muted)}
  .ag-cal i{width:7px;height:7px;border-radius:50%;display:block}
  .empty{padding:40px;text-align:center;color:var(--faint)}

  /* ── popovers / modals ─────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  #detail{position:fixed;z-index:60;width:330px;background:var(--overlay);border:1px solid var(--border-strong);
    border-radius:14px;box-shadow:0 24px 60px rgba(0,0,0,.55);display:none;overflow:hidden}
  #detail.open{display:block}
  #detail .bar{height:5px;background:var(--cc)}
  #detail .body{padding:14px}
  #detail h3{margin:0 0 2px;font-size:15px;line-height:1.3}
  #detail .when{font-size:12px;color:var(--muted);margin-bottom:10px}
  #detail .field{font-size:12px;color:var(--muted);display:flex;gap:8px;margin-top:8px;line-height:1.5}
  #detail .field span:first-child{width:16px;flex:0 0 auto;text-align:center;opacity:.7}
  #detail .calchips{display:flex;gap:4px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-top:10px}
  #detail .calchip{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:5px;font-size:10px;padding:2px 7px;
    border-radius:999px;border:1px solid var(--border);color:var(--muted)}
  #detail .calchip i{width:6px;height:6px;border-radius:50%;display:block}
  #detail .actions{display:flex;gap:6px;justify-content:flex-end;padding:10px 14px;
    border-top:1px solid var(--border);background:var(--raised)}

  .backdrop{position:fixed;inset:0;background:rgba(0,0,0,.55);backdrop-filter:blur(2px);
    z-index:70;display:none;align-items:center;justify-content:center;padding:20px}
  .backdrop.open{display:flex}
  .modal{width:min(560px,100%);max-height:90vh;overflow:auto;background:var(--overlay);
    border:1px solid var(--border-strong);border-radius:16px;box-shadow:0 30px 80px rgba(0,0,0,.6)}
  .modal header{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;padding:14px 18px;
    border-bottom:1px solid var(--border)}
  .modal header h2{margin:0;font-size:15px}
  .modal .content{padding:16px 18px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:12px}
  .modal footer{display:flex;gap:8px;justify-content:flex-end;padding:12px 18px;
    border-top:1px solid var(--border);background:var(--raised)}
  .row{display:flex;gap:10px}
  .row > *{flex:1;min-width:0}
  label.f{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:4px;font-size:11px;color:var(--muted);font-weight:600}
  label.f input,label.f select,label.f textarea{
    background:var(--sunken);border:1px solid var(--border-strong);border-radius:8px;
    padding:8px 10px;font-size:13px;color:var(--text);font-weight:400;width:100%;
  }
  label.f input:focus,label.f select:focus,label.f textarea:focus{outline:2px solid var(--primary);outline-offset:-1px}
  label.f textarea{resize:vertical;min-height:58px}
  .checkbox{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font-size:12px;color:var(--muted)}
  .checkbox input{width:15px;height:15px;accent-color:var(--primary)}
  .calpick{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:6px}
  .calpick label{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;font-size:11px;padding:5px 9px;
    border:1px solid var(--border-strong);border-radius:999px;cursor:pointer;color:var(--muted)}
  .calpick label.on{border-color:var(--cc);background:color-mix(in oklch,var(--cc) 22%, transparent);color:var(--text)}
  .calpick input{display:none}
  .calpick i{width:7px;height:7px;border-radius:50%;display:block}
  .swatches{display:flex;gap:6px;flex-wrap:wrap}
  .swatches button{width:22px;height:22px;border-radius:50%;border:2px solid transparent}
  .swatches button.on{border-color:var(--text)}
  .err{color:var(--error);font-size:11px;min-height:0}

  /* ── notifications ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  #notif-panel{
    position:fixed;top:52px;right:12px;width:390px;max-height:min(70vh,560px);z-index:80;
    background:var(--overlay);border:1px solid var(--border-strong);border-radius:14px;
    box-shadow:0 24px 60px rgba(0,0,0,.55);display:none;flex-direction:column;overflow:hidden;
  }
  #notif-panel.open{display:flex}
  #notif-panel header{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;padding:10px 12px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--border)}
  #notif-panel header h3{margin:0;font-size:13px;flex:1}
  .tabs{display:flex;gap:2px;padding:8px 12px 0}
  .tabs button{font-size:11px;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:7px;color:var(--muted)}
  .tabs button[aria-selected="true"]{background:var(--raised);color:var(--text);font-weight:600}
  .nlist{overflow:auto;padding:6px}
  .nitem{display:flex;gap:9px;padding:9px;border-radius:9px;cursor:pointer;align-items:flex-start}
  .nitem:hover{background:var(--raised)}
  .nitem .ico{width:20px;flex:0 0 auto;text-align:center;font-size:12px;padding-top:1px}
  .nitem .txt{flex:1;min-width:0}
  .nitem .ttl{font-size:12px;font-weight:600;display:flex;gap:6px;align-items:center}
  .nitem .sub{font-size:11px;color:var(--faint);margin-top:2px;line-height:1.45}
  .nitem .when{font-size:10px;color:var(--faint);font-family:var(--mono);white-space:nowrap}
  .nitem.unread .ttl::before{content:"";width:6px;height:6px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--primary);flex:0 0 auto}
  .nitem.missed{background:color-mix(in oklch,var(--warning) 9%, transparent)}
  .nfooter{border-top:1px solid var(--border);padding:8px 12px;display:flex;gap:8px;justify-content:space-between}

  /* ── toasts / reminder popups ──────────────────────────────────────── */
  #toasts{position:fixed;right:16px;bottom:16px;z-index:90;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:10px;
    width:360px;max-width:calc(100vw - 32px)}
  .toast{background:var(--overlay);border:1px solid var(--border-strong);border-radius:14px;
    box-shadow:0 20px 50px rgba(0,0,0,.6);overflow:hidden;animation:slidein .18s ease-out}
  @keyframes slidein{from{transform:translateY(12px);opacity:0}to{transform:translateY(0);opacity:1}}
  .toast .bar{height:4px;background:var(--primary)}
  .toast .in{padding:12px 14px}
  .toast .kick{font-size:10px;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.1em;color:var(--primary);
    font-weight:700;display:flex;gap:6px;align-items:center}
  .toast h4{margin:6px 0 2px;font-size:14px}
  .toast p{margin:0;font-size:12px;color:var(--muted);line-height:1.45}
  .toast .acts{display:flex;gap:6px;padding:0 14px 12px}
  .toast .acts .btn{font-size:11px;padding:5px 10px}
  .sr{position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;overflow:hidden;clip:rect(0 0 0 0)}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<div id="app">
  <div class="topbar">
    <div class="brand"><span class="dot"></span>codx-junior <small>calendar</small></div>
    <button class="btn" id="btn-today">Today</button>
    <button class="btn icon" id="btn-prev" title="Previous (←)">‹</button>
    <button class="btn icon" id="btn-next" title="Next (→)">›</button>
    <div id="range-label">—</div>
    <div class="spacer"></div>
    <div class="sim" title="Simulated clock: reminders fire from this clock, not the real one">
      <span>sim</span><b id="sim-clock">--:--</b>
      <button class="btn" id="sim-play" title="Toggle time flow">❚❚</button>
      <button class="btn" id="sim-next" title="Jump to the next pending reminder">⏭ next</button>
      <button class="btn" id="sim-reset" title="Back to real time">now</button>
    </div>
    <div class="seg" role="tablist" id="view-switch">
      <button role="tab" data-view="month" aria-selected="true">Month</button>
      <button role="tab" data-view="week" aria-selected="false">Week</button>
      <button role="tab" data-view="day" aria-selected="false">Day</button>
      <button role="tab" data-view="agenda" aria-selected="false">Agenda</button>
    </div>
    <button class="bell" id="btn-bell" title="Notifications">
      <span aria-hidden="true">🔔</span>
      <span class="badge" id="notif-badge" hidden>0</span>
    </button>
    <button class="btn primary" id="btn-new">+ New event</button>
  </div>

  <aside>
    <button class="create" id="btn-create"><span class="plus">+</span> Create</button>
    <div class="mini" id="mini"></div>
    <div>
      <div class="section-title">My calendars</div>
      <div class="cal-list" id="cal-list"></div>
      <button class="cal-row" id="btn-add-cal" style="color:var(--primary);font-weight:600">
        <span style="width:14px;text-align:center">+</span> Add calendar
      </button>
    </div>
    <div>
      <div class="section-title">Other calendars</div>
      <div class="cal-list" id="cal-list-other"></div>
    </div>
    <div class="spacer"></div>
    <details class="help">
      <summary>About this prototype</summary>
      <ul>
        <li>Open a cell to create an event; click a chip for details.</li>
        <li><b>Work · Personal · Team</b> are editable calendars. <b>codx-junior</b> is a read-only
          projection of tasks, runs and meets.</li>
        <li>“Sprint 42 review” lives in <b>two</b> calendars: the chip shows a two-tone bar and both dots.</li>
        <li>Reminders fire from the <b>simulated clock</b>: use ❚❚ / ⏭ next.</li>
        <li>Keys: <kbd>n</kbd> new · <kbd>t</kbd> today · <kbd>m</kbd><kbd>w</kbd><kbd>d</kbd><kbd>a</kbd>
          views · <kbd>←</kbd><kbd>→</kbd> move · <kbd>Esc</kbd> close.</li>
        <li>Data is demo data kept in localStorage. <button class="btn ghost" id="btn-reset"
          style="padding:0;font-size:11px;color:var(--error);text-decoration:underline">Reset demo data</button></li>
      </ul>
    </details>
  </aside>

  <main id="view"></main>
</div>

<div id="detail" role="dialog" aria-label="Event details"></div>

<div class="backdrop" id="backdrop">
  <div class="modal" id="modal" role="dialog" aria-modal="true"></div>
</div>

<div id="notif-panel" role="dialog" aria-label="Notifications"></div>

<div id="toasts" aria-live="polite"></div>

<script>
"use strict";
/* ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   0. tiny date layer
   The prototype stores NAIVE LOCAL iso strings ("2026-02-10T09:00") so the
   demo is stable in any timezone. The real API stores UTC + the calendar's
   timezone and returns occurrences (analysis §8).
   ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
const MIN = 60000, HOUR = 3600000, DAY = 86400000;
const DOW = ["Mon","Tue","Wed","Thu","Fri","Sat","Sun"];
const DOW_LONG = ["Monday","Tuesday","Wednesday","Thursday","Friday","Saturday","Sunday"];
const MON = ["January","February","March","April","May","June","July","August","September","October","November","December"];
const pad2 = n => String(n).padStart(2, "0");
const pdate = iso => iso ? new Date(iso) : null;                 // naive-local iso -> Date
function isoLocal(d){
  return `${d.getFullYear()}-${pad2(d.getMonth()+1)}-${pad2(d.getDate())}T${pad2(d.getHours())}:${pad2(d.getMinutes())}`;
}
const dateKey = d => `${d.getFullYear()}-${pad2(d.getMonth()+1)}-${pad2(d.getDate())}`;
const startOfDay = d => new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate());
const addDays = (d, n) => new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate()+n, d.getHours(), d.getMinutes());
const addMonths = (d, n) => new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth()+n, 1);
function startOfWeek(d){ const s = startOfDay(d); const w = (s.getDay()+6)%7; return addDays(s, -w); }
const sameDay = (a,b) => a.getFullYear()===b.getFullYear() && a.getMonth()===b.getMonth() && a.getDate()===b.getDate();
const daysBetween = (a,b) => Math.round((startOfDay(b) - startOfDay(a))/DAY);
function fmtTime(d){ return `${pad2(d.getHours())}:${pad2(d.getMinutes())}`; }
function fmtTimeRange(a,b){ return `${fmtTime(a)} – ${fmtTime(b)}`; }
function fmtDay(d){ return `${DOW_LONG[(d.getDay()+6)%7]}, ${d.getDate()} ${MON[d.getMonth()]} ${d.getFullYear()}`; }
function fmtShort(d){ return `${DOW[(d.getDay()+6)%7]} ${d.getDate()} ${MON[d.getMonth()].slice(0,3)}`; }

/* ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

         recurrence:{ rrule:"FREQ=MONTHLY;INTERVAL=1;UNTIL:" + isoLocal(addDays(today,180)).replace(/[-:]/g,"").slice(0,8) + "T235959Z" } }),

         start:isoLocal(addDays(today,14))+"T00:00", end:isoLocal(addDays(today,15))+"T00:00",
