## 6. The `codx-junior` calendar (R5 + R6)

A virtual calendar, visible from every project, **read-only**. It is the one thing
that deliberately crosses project boundaries (D1): its items depict **every project
the viewer can open**. Nothing is stored — it is computed on read.

| Source | Rule | Badge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Task with `scheduled_start/end` | Block at that time, in the task's own project. | `Task` |
| Task with `due_date`, no schedule | All-day marker on the due date; `overdue` styling if `due < today` and `status != done`. | `Due` |
| Orchestration run (`run_id`, `run_status`) | Block from `started_at`, or all-day if not started. | `Run` |
| Meet | Block at the scheduled time (needs the new `Meet.scheduled_start`, §11). | `Meet` |

Properties:

- **Not writable.** Dragging a `codx-junior` item moves the *task*, in the project
  that owns it (`PUT /api/planning/tasks/{id}`, resolved from the item's
  `project_id`), not an event. This is the behaviour that makes the calendar
  useful instead of a second task board.
- **Filterable** by project (§5.2), source, board, sprint, assignee and status
  (the query's `projects` + `sources` + `boards` fields), reusing the planning
  filters.
- **Multi-calendar**: a task shows *simultaneously* in `codx-junior` and in any
  calendar in its `calendar_ids`. Adding it to "Work" does not duplicate it; it
  is one task with two memberships, so completing it clears both.
- **Same title, different projects = different items.** Two `project_id`s, two
  chips, and the chip tooltip / agenda row carry the project badge so they are
  never confused.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    T1[Chat / task<br/>project A<br/>scheduled_start, calendar_ids=['cal_work']]
    T2[Chat / task<br/>project B]
    T1 --> P[Projection<br/>projects[] filter, capped]
    T2 --> P
    P --> SYS[codx-junior calendar<br/>system, read-only, all projects]
    P --> W[Work calendar<br/>via calendar_ids]
    W -->|drag / resize| API[PUT /api/planning/tasks/:id<br/>resolved by project_id]
    SYS -->|drag / resize| API
```

## 7. Notifications and popup reminders (R3 + R4)

### 7.1 Pipeline

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant BG as Background thread (30 s)
    participant ST as calendar store
    participant SIO as Socket.IO (broadcast)
    participant CL as Client store/calendar.js
    participant UI as NotificationCentre + popup

    BG->>ST: load events in [now-1d, now+7d]
    BG->>BG: expand occurrences, compute trigger_at = start - minutes
    BG->>ST: read delivered.json
    BG->>BG: due = trigger_at <= now and not delivered
    BG->>ST: append to delivered.json (atomic)
    BG->>SIO: emit codx-junior-calendar-reminder {occurrence, minutes_before}
    SIO->>CL: event
    CL->>UI: push notification + show popup card
    UI->>ST: POST /events/{id}/snooze  (optional)
```

### 7.2 Why a background thread and not "the browser sets a timeout"

The browser timer is the easy path and it is wrong: it dies with the tab, it
cannot deliver when the app is closed, and a laptop asleep at 09:45 never fires
the 10:00 reminder. The server tick also makes email/Web-Push a later plug-in
instead of a rewrite.

It still degrades gracefully: if the tick runs while nobody is connected, the
reminder is **marked delivered and persisted**, so the notification centre shows
it as "missed" the next time the client loads (`GET /api/calendar/reminders?since=`).

### 7.3 Delivery dedupe

`delivered.json`:

```json
{ "evt_01JQ8Z…|2026-02-10T09:00:00Z|15": "2026-02-10T08:45:03Z" }
```

Key = `event_id|occurrence_start|minutes_before`. Bounded: entries older than 30
days are pruned on every tick (≈ 3 events/day → a few hundred lines). Exactly the
same trick as the harness `notification_sent` flag (see
`api/tests/harness/test_harness_notification.py`: "must be sent exactly once …
the durable flag survives duplicate ticks/restarts").

### 7.4 Client side

- `store/calendar.js` (new Vuex module) holds `calendars`, `occurrences`,
  `notifications[]` (**persistent**, unlike `ui.notifications`), `unreadCount`.
- Socket handler registered once at `init()`:
  `API.socket.on('codx-junior-calendar-reminder', …)` (the `SocketManager.on`
  keeps named listeners across reconnects — verified in `api/socket.js`).
- `components/calendar/ReminderPopup.vue` — bottom-right card: title, time,
  "Snooze 5 / 10 min", "Dismiss", "Open". Auto-dismiss after 60 s **without**
  losing the notification-centre entry.
- `components/Notifications.vue` gains a third section ("Reminders") plus
  unread/read state. The transient `ui.addNotification` toasts stay for
  operational messages (they are not a reminder channel).
- Browser `Notification` API: **opt-in** toggle in the calendar settings, used
  only when the tab is backgrounded. Requires HTTPS/localhost.
- M3 extension: Web Push (service worker + VAPID) and email; both plug into the
  same tick, which is why the design keeps delivery out of the request path.

## 8. Recurrence and timezones

### 8.1 Model

Store **RFC 5545 RRULE** as a string, plus exceptions — the same shape Google
Calendar and ICS use, so export is lossless:

```json
"recurrence": {
  "rrule": "FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=1;BYDAY=MO,WE;UNTIL=20260630T000000Z",
  "exdates": ["2026-03-04T09:00:00Z"],
  "overrides": {
    "2026-03-11T09:00:00Z": { "start": "2026-03-11T14:00:00Z", "end": "2026-03-11T15:00:00Z", "title": "Spec review (moved)" }
  }
}
```

`overrides` keys are the *original* occurrence starts, i.e. `RECURRENCE-ID` in
ICS terms — a straight mapping.

### 8.2 Expansion rules (server)

- Expand only inside the requested range, hard-capped at
  `MAX_OCCURRENCES = 750` per event and a 2-year horizon (`invalid_recurrence`
  beyond that).
- Everything is computed in the **event's** timezone, then serialised as UTC.
  This is what makes `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO` stay at 09:00 local across a DST
  change instead of drifting to 08:00/10:00 as a naive UTC expansion does.
- `UNTIL` is inclusive; `COUNT` counts generated instances.

### 8.3 Dependencies (verified)

| Need | Today | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RRULE parsing/expansion (Python) | `python-dateutil` is **not** a declared dependency in `api/pyproject.toml` | Add `python-dateutil>=2.9` (pure-python, MIT, tiny). It ships `dateutil.rrule`, the reference implementation. |
| ICS import/export | not present | Add `icalendar>=6.0` (pure python). Alternatively hand-write the (small) VEVENT/VTIMEZONE subset — decide in M2. |
| Client recurrence | `moment` only (no `moment-timezone`, no `rrule`) | Not needed: the server returns occurrences. |
| Client timezone display | `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in the browser | Use it; no new client dependency. |

> Rule of thumb for this feature: **the browser never does date maths**. It
> formats what the API gives it. That is how the prototype is built too.

2. **Source badge, not colour, marks provenance.** `Task`, `Due`, `Run`, `Meet`

7. **Mobile**: the month grid becomes the default; day/agenda replace week; the

## 10. Interoperability — an explicit non-goal

**Google Calendar is not integrated** (decision D4). It was named in the request
as a *design reference* — the interaction model this document copies — not as a
system to sync with. So, deliberately:

| Not built | Why it stays out |
| --- | --- |
| Google OAuth | No account to link. `security/github_oauth.py` remains the only OAuth implementation. |
| `icalendar` / `python-dateutil` as **required** deps | Both are still absent from `api/pyproject.toml` (verified). If they are ever added it must be for a dated need, not "maybe ICS". |
| Incremental sync, `syncToken`, `watch` channels | The expensive parts of the problem, and they buy nothing until there is an account to sync. |
| Free/busy across accounts, Gmail invitations | Same. |

What is left, optionally and with **zero new dependencies**:

| Optional nice-to-have | Scope | Effort |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **ICS export** (`GET /api/calendar/feed/{calendar_id}.ics?token=…`, token = HMAC of `calendar_id + user`) | Lets a user add their codx-junior calendar to *any* external client (Apple, Thunderbird, Google) without us ever calling an external API. A serialiser for `VEVENT` is ~60 lines. | S |
| **ICS import** (`POST /api/calendar/import`, idempotent by `UID`) | Symmetric, and it validates the `external` scope we already model. | M |

Neither is a milestone. Ship them only if a user asks for a feed; the data model
already supports them (`external` scope, `refs.external_uid`).

## 11. Multi-user, permissions, and scheduling meets

Because the store is **global** (D1) and calendars can be **private or shared**
(D2), the ACL is resolved **per request** and never baked into the files.

### 11.1 Who sees which calendar

```
viewer ──▶ for each calendar in calendars.json:
            scope == 'private'   → owner == viewer.username
            scope == 'team'      → membership in audience (team <project>/<name>
                                    resolved live via the team manager)
            scope == 'workspace' → true (any authenticated user)
            scope == 'system'    → true, read_only
            scope == 'external'  → true, read_only
```

| Role in `members[]` | Read | Write / delete | Share |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `owner` | yes | yes | yes (change `scope`/`audience` too) |
| `writer` | yes | yes | no |
| `reader` | yes | **no** (403 `read_only_calendar`) | no |
| not a member | **no** (the calendar is not returned at all) | no | no |
| global admin | yes | yes | yes |

Rules that matter:

- A **private** calendar of another user must never appear in a list, a count, a
  search result or an error message — "not found" and "not allowed" are the same
  404. The fixture asserts this for `marta` and `bob`
  (`expected_visibility`).
- **Events inherit** the ACL of their calendars; `visibility: private` in the
  document masks title ("Private"), description, location and guests for viewers
  who are neither the creator nor a `writer`, while keeping the time slot —
  overlapping meetings stay visible (`expected_private_masking`).
- `system`/`external` calendars are `read_only` for everyone, including admins.
- The reminder thread runs **once for the whole installation** and fans out to the
  recipients of each calendar (§7.1), so a private calendar's reminder goes only
  to its owner.

### 11.2 Scheduling a meet from the calendar (D3)

`Meet` (`api/codx/junior/meets/model.py`) has no `scheduled_start`: it is a *live
room*, not an appointment. Since the calendar **is** the place to schedule a meet,
we add the appointment to it:

```python
# api/codx/junior/meets/model.py — additive, defaulted
scheduled_start: Optional[str] = None
scheduled_end:   Optional[str] = None
calendar_ids:    List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
project_id:      Optional[str] = None
```

and one endpoint that writes both halves in a single transaction:

```
POST /api/meets/schedule   {title, start, end, calendar_ids[], project_id?, guests[]}
  → creates the Meet (scheduled_start/end, calendar_ids)
  → creates the linked CalendarEvent (refs.meet_id, location "Meet /meet/<id>")
  → returns {meet, event}
  → 409 meet_already_scheduled if the meet has scheduled_start already
```

This closes a real weakness rather than adding one: `MeetManager` keeps meets in
`self._meets` (a dict) and **loses them on restart**, so "a meeting at 15:00
tomorrow" is impossible today. After D3 the calendar event is the durable record
and the meet can be rehydrated from it. Deleting the event cancels the schedule
but keeps the meet; deleting the meet deletes the event (`refs.meet_id`).

| `POST /events/query` month view (3 shards, 3 calendars, ~500 occurrences) | < 60 ms p95 |

| Reminder tick (one thread, whole installation) | < 50 ms; ≤ 7 days of events loaded |
| Socket payload for a reminder | < 2 KB |

## 13. Accessibility

- Grid is a real table-semantics structure (`role="grid"`, `aria-rowcount`,
  cells focusable, arrow-key navigation between days).
- Chips are `<button>` with `aria-label="Spec review, 10:00–11:00, Work"`.
- Colour is never the only signal: every chip also carries its calendar's initial
  or a dot pattern, so the magenta/green pair is distinguishable for
  deuteranopia (the brand palette's magenta↔green pair is a known risky pair —

- Reminder popup: `role="alert"`, focusable actions, no auto-dismiss when

## 14. Test strategy

| Level | What |
| --- | --- |
| Unit (Python) | Store round-trip; atomic write under a simulated crash; month-shard boundary; recurrence expansion incl. DST boundary and `COUNT`/`UNTIL`; reminder dedupe across two ticks and a restart. |
| Unit (JS) | Occurrence layout (overlap lanes), chip density ("+N more"), view range maths. |
| API | Query contract with the fixture; `revision_mismatch`; `read_only_calendar`; ACL for a `reader`. |
| Integration | Task with `calendar_ids` shows in two calendars and in `codx-junior`; editing it in the calendar goes through the planning endpoint. |
| E2E (browser profile) | Create a calendar → create an event with a reminder → advance the server clock → assert the popup and the notification centre. |
| Prototype | `02-prototype/index.html` is the visual acceptance artefact for the UX review. |

Fixtures: `03-fixtures/calendar-fixture.json` (version 2) — 6 calendars, 8
events, 3 tasks in 3 different projects, 1 run, 1 scheduled meet. It carries

| Key | Asserts |
| --- | --- |
| `expected_query` | 12 occurrences in the anchor week, with the recurrence override expanded and every `project_id` intact. |
| `expected_filters` | `projects[]` semantics: `codx-junior-platform` 9, `acme-web` 2, `personal` 1, `acme-web+personal` 3, `internal-wiki` 1, empty 12 = the unfiltered total. |
| `expected_visibility` | The same request as `alice` / `marta` / `jordi` / `bob`: private calendars of another user are never returned, a `reader` cannot write. |
| `expected_private_masking` | A `visibility: private` event keeps its slot but masks title/description/location/guests for other viewers. |
| `expected_reminders` | 5 triggers in the window with their exact `trigger_at` (incl. a task inheriting its calendar's default reminder), 1 occurrence outside it, the `event_id\|occurrence_start\|minutes_before` dedupe key, and per-owner delivery. |

Every total is derived from the data, not copied: the three disjoint project
filters (9 + 2 + 1) add up to the unfiltered 12.
---

## 15. Risks

| # | Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Task projection drifts from the Task Manager | Users see two truths | One single projection function, server-side; the calendar **never** writes task fields except through the planning API. |
| 2 | `due_date` vs `scheduled_*` confusion | Wrong priority/overdue logic | Keep both, document them, draw `due` as an all-day deadline marker (§6). |
| 3 | Reminder duplicates / losses | Trust damage | Persisted dedupe key + restart test; 30 s tick with a `now-1d` look-back window. |
| 4 | Timezone/DST bugs in recurrence | Meetings one hour off | Compute in the event timezone, store UTC, test the DST weekend explicitly. |
| 5 | Unbounded recurrence expansion | Latency spike | `MAX_OCCURRENCES`, 92-day query cap, 2-year horizon. |
| 6 | Scope creep back to Google sync | A milestone becomes unbounded | D4 in §1.1: Google is a non-goal. A pull request that adds an OAuth flow for it is out of scope until a user asks. |
| 7 | Notification fatigue | Users mute everything | Per-calendar reminder defaults, max 2 reminders per event, quiet hours in `settings.json`. |
| 8 | Board/planning regressions | Broken Task Manager | New `Chat` fields are additive with defaults; the planning tests must stay green before merging. |
| 9 | The existing `SolopreneurCalendar.vue` mock confuses readers | Wrong screen maintained | It is deleted/pointed at the real store in M1 (it is mock-only, verified). |

---

| Milestone | Content | Acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **M0 — global foundations** (≈ 4–5 days) | `CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH` in `globals.py`; `calendar/store.py` copying `CompanyStore`; `Calendar` with `scope/owner/audience` + per-request ACL; `api/calendar.py` (calendars, prefs, `projects[]` query, events CRUD); `store/calendar.js`; `views/CalendarView.vue` with the **project filter**, month/week/day/agenda and the scope-grouped sidebar. `Chat.calendar_ids/scheduled_*`. | Two users: `marta` never sees `Work`/`Personal`; a team calendar is readable by a `reader` and not writable; switching the project filter changes the counts exactly as `expected_filters`; fixture tests green. |
| **M1 — projection + writes + meets** (≈ 4 days) | `codx-junior` projection across the filtered projects (§4.6, cache + cap), drag & resize writing back through the planning endpoint with `project_id`, `Meet.scheduled_*` + `POST /api/meets/schedule` (D3), editor modal with guests and a project selector. | Dragging a task chip reschedules the task **in its own project**; a scheduled meet appears on the calendar and survives a restart. |
| **M2 — reminders + notifications** (≈ 3 days) | One background ticker for the installation, `delivered.json` per recipient, socket event, notification centre (unread/read/missed), `ReminderPopup.vue`, snooze, opt-in browser notifications. | Reminder fires exactly once, survives a restart, appears in the centre after being missed, and a private calendar's reminder reaches only its owner. |
| **M3 — recurrence** (≈ 4 days) | RRULE + overrides, per-instance edit/delete. | A weekly event keeps 09:00 across the DST change; moving one instance leaves the series intact. |
| **Optional — ICS export/import** (≈ 1 day) | Only if asked (§10). No new mandatory dependency. | A exported `.ics` opens in any client. |

and the scheduler exist. Google moved out of the plan entirely (D4).

## 0. TL;DR — the decision

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Scope | **Global (installation-wide)**: a user works on several projects and needs **one** agenda. Projects are a **filter**, never a namespace (D1). |
| Where does the data live? | `<CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH>` (default `/home/codx-junior/calendar`), beside `companies/` and `analytics/` — JSON written atomically, copying `company/store.py`. **Not** inside the project `.codx`, **not** inside chat/board documents. |
| How many calendars? | Unlimited, global. Each has a colour, timezone, default reminders and a **scope**: `private` / `team` / `workspace` (D2). |
| Who sees what? | Resolved per request from `CodxUser` + team membership + calendar ACL. A private calendar never leaks; a `reader` can read a team calendar but not write it (§11). |
| How does a task appear in several calendars? | The **item** owns the list of calendars (`calendar_ids[]`), not the calendar. A task is *always* in the system calendar `codx-junior` and *optionally* pinned to N user calendars. |
| What is the `codx-junior` calendar? | A **virtual, read-only system calendar** whose items project task/run/meet data **from every project the viewer can see**. Computed on read, never stored. |
| How are projects reconciled? | Every event and every projected item carries `project_id` (nullable = personal). The API takes `projects[]`, the UI shows a project filter. Empty filter = all projects. |
| Can the calendar schedule a meet? | **Yes** (D3). A meet scheduled ahead is a calendar event, and `Meet.scheduled_start/end` is the durable record — which also fixes `MeetManager` being in-memory only. |
| Who expands recurrences and timezones? | The **server** returns *occurrences*, not events (precedent: `planning_manager.py` already derives flags/counts server-side). The client only renders. |
| How do reminders fire? | A background thread in `background.py` ticks every 30 s, dedupes through a persisted `delivered.json`, and emits a socket event. The client turns it into a toast + entry in the notification centre. |
| Google Calendar? | **Out of scope** (D4). Google was a design reference, not an integration. §10 is kept as a documented non-goal; ICS export is the only optional escape hatch. |
| Effort | 4 milestones, §16. M0 (global store + private/team calendars + filters + task projection) is the useful 60 %. |

| id | Requirement |

| R2 | Create **multiple calendars** with own colour/visibility (Google Calendar behaviour). |

| R8 | Recurring events. |

| R12 | Deep analysis + prototype **before** any change (this document + prototype). |

### 3.1 Calendar

```json

  "timezone": "Europe/Madrid",
  "read_only": false,
  "provider": "local",
  "default_reminders": [{ "channel": "popup", "minutes_before": 10 }],
  "members": [{ "user": "alice", "role": "owner" }],
  "visible": true,
  "order": 0,
  "created_at": "2026-02-01T09:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-02-01T09:00:00Z"

```

`scope` drives behaviour. There is no `kind`/`project` calendar any more: since
the store is **global** (D1), a calendar is not owned by a project.

| scope | Who sees it | Who writes | `audience` | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `private` | **only `owner`** | `owner` | `null` | "Work", "Personal" |
| `team` | the members of one team | `owner` + `writer` members | `{kind:"team", project, name, members[]}` | "Team — Platform" |
| `workspace` | every authenticated user | `owner` or a global admin | `{kind:"workspace"}` | "All hands" |
| `system` | every authenticated user | **nobody** (virtual) | `{kind:"workspace"}` | `codx-junior` |
| `external` | every authenticated user | the sync job | `{kind:"workspace"}` | "Holidays (ICS)" |

A `team` calendar names its team as `<project>/<team>` because teams live in the
project control plane (`.codx/teams/`), while the calendar itself is global. That
qualified name is the only coupling between the two worlds — no copying of
membership, resolved on read through the existing team manager.

> **Personal events and projects.** A private calendar is *not* a project: an event
> with `project_id: null` belongs to the user, matches the `personal` filter token
> and appears in the agenda of any project context.

### 3.2 CalendarEvent

```json
{

  "calendar_ids": ["cal_work", "cal_personal"],
  "project_id": "codx-junior-platform",
  "title": "Spec review — calendar manager",
  "description": "Walk through §4 storage + §7 reminders.",
  "location": "Meet /meet/9f2a",
  "start": "2026-02-10T09:00:00Z",
  "end": "2026-02-10T10:00:00Z",
  "all_day": false,
  "timezone": "Europe/Madrid",
  "recurrence": null,
  "reminders": [
    { "channel": "popup", "minutes_before": 15 },
    { "channel": "popup", "minutes_before": 0 }
  ],
  "status": "confirmed",
  "visibility": "default",
  "source": "native",
  "refs": {},
  "guests": ["marta"],
  "created_by": "alice",
  "created_at": "2026-02-03T10:12:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-02-03T10:12:00Z",
  "revision": 1
}
```

**Invariants**

1. `calendar_ids` is non-empty, deduplicated, and every id must resolve to an
   existing calendar (validated on write; a dangling id is returned by
   `GET /calendars?orphans=1` for repair, never silently dropped).
2. A `system` or `external` calendar can never appear alone in
   `calendar_ids` in a *write*: content coming from a projection cannot be
   edited (409 `read_only_calendar`).
3. `end > start` unless `all_day` (then `end = start + 1 day` inclusive-exclusive).
4. `revision` is incremented on every write; clients send `If-Match` (§5.3).
5. A recurring event stores the **first** `start`; instances are computed.
6. A recurring event **cannot span calendars differently per instance** (a
   Google limitation we intentionally keep: it removes a whole class of bugs).

## 4. Storage design

### 4.1 Layout

```
${CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH:-/home/codx-junior/calendar}/
├── calendars.json                 # [Calendar]  — small, single document, ALL users
├── events/
│   ├── 2026-01.json               # [CalendarEvent] keyed by start month (UTC)
│   ├── 2026-02.json
│   └── 2026-03.json
├── delivered.json                 # reminder dedupe, per recipient (see §7.3)
├── prefs/<username>.json          # that user's hidden calendars, order, week start
└── export/
    └── cal_work.ics               # generated feed, on demand
```

Three things moved compared with the per-project draft:

| was (per project) | is (global) | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<codx_path>/calendar/` | `$CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH` | `<codx_path>` is `<project>/.codx` (`project_manager.create_project`): one store per project means the same calendar in N places. |
| `settings.json` shared | `prefs/<username>.json` | Visibility and order are **per user**; a shared settings file makes two users fight over one JSON. |
| `export/` git-ignored | generated on request | Nothing is committed anywhere. |

The path goes into `api/codx/junior/globals.py` beside the existing global
folders, so it is overridable in containers and tests:

```python
# Global path for the calendar store, shared across all projects.
CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH = os.environ.get(
    "CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH", "/home/codx-junior/calendar"
)
```

### 4.2 Why not store this on the Chat / board document?

- A board document is rewritten wholesale on every card move; adding events
  there would multiply write amplification and lock contention.
- Events are **not** tasks: they have guests, recurrence and reminders, and they
  must be queryable by date range across the whole project.
- Tasks only ever *project* into the calendar. Keeping the projection read-only
  guarantees that the Task Manager stays the single writer of task data.

**Not inside the project either** (D1). `<codx_path>` is *the project's* `.codx`
(`settings.codx_path = f"{project_path}/.codx"` in `project_manager.py`), so a
per-project store would mean:

- the same "Team — Platform" calendar existing once per project, diverging;
- a reminder firing N times, once per project copy;
- a personal calendar that disappears when you switch project — exactly what the
  requirement rules out.

The precedent already exists twice in the codebase: `ANALYTICS_DATA_PATH` and
`API_LOGS_DATA_PATH` are documented as *"Global path … shared across all projects"*,
and `CODX_JUNIOR_COMPANIES_PATH` keeps hybrid organizations in a global folder.
The calendar joins that family.

### 4.3 Conventions copied from `company/store.py`

`CompanyStore` is the closest existing thing: a **global** root, one document per
entity, atomic write and a per-entity lock. Copy it instead of inventing one.

- **Root resolution**: env var → `codx.junior.globals` → default constant, exactly
  like `get_companies_root()`.
- **Atomic write**: temp file in the same directory → `flush` → `fsync` →
  `os.replace`. A crash can never leave half a month file.
- **Cross-process exclusion**: `fcntl.flock` on `calendar/.lock` while a write is
  in flight (the API runs several uvicorn workers — see the comment in
  `pyproject.toml` about multi-worker deployments), falling back to a thread lock
  when `fcntl` is unavailable, like `CompanyStore.lock`.
- **Bounded, validated ids**: `os.path.basename()` on every id before building a
  path, like `CompanyStore.company_dir`.
- **Tolerant reads**: a corrupt month file is logged and skipped; the calendar
  still renders (never a 500 because of one bad file).

### 4.4 Month sharding and the overlap problem

Query windows are small by nature (month view = 3 shards, week = 2, agenda = 2).
A long event (holiday, offsite) may start before the window and overlap into it.
Rule:

> An event is stored in the shard of its **start** month, and a range query reads
> `[from - MAX_EVENT_DURATION, to]` where `MAX_EVENT_DURATION = 31 days`.
> Events longer than 31 days are rejected on write (400 `event_too_long`); a
> "long" period must be a recurring event or an all-day per-day block.

This keeps every query at ≤ 4 file reads with no index to maintain. The shards
are now **global** (every user, every project), so the threshold arrives sooner:
past ~20 k events add `events/index.json`
(`{id, month, start, end, calendar_ids, project_id}`) — the documented escape
hatch, not part of M0.

### 4.5 Size budget

| Item | Estimate |
| --- | --- |
| Calendar | ~400 B |
| Event (with description) | ~1 KB |
| 2 000 events / year / **installation** | ≈ 2 MB total, ≈ 170 KB per shard |

Comfortably JSON. No database, no migration of existing data.

### 4.6 Cross-project projection cost (the price of D1)

The `codx-junior` calendar is the only part that must look **outside** the global
store, because tasks live in each project's `.codx`. That is the one real cost the
global decision adds, and it is bounded:

| Concern | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Which projects? | `CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH` (`globals.py`) → project folders; keep only those the viewer can open (`CodxUser.projects`, `ProjectPermission`, `children`). Never read a project the viewer cannot access. |
| How many at once? | The projects in the current filter, capped (`MAX_PROJECTS_PER_QUERY = 12`). An unfiltered request projects the 12 most recently touched and says so in the response (`truncated_projects`). |
| Cost per project | Reuse the existing per-project task read (`task_manager` / kanban store). No new file format, no cross-project index. |
| Cache | In-process dict keyed by `(project_id, mtime of its task store)`; an unchanged project is not re-read. Rebuildable, like the `RUNTIME_FOLDER` caches. |
| Failure | A project that fails to read is skipped and reported in `warnings[]`; one broken project never blanks the agenda. |
| Write path | None. Dragging a projected item calls the planning endpoint **in that item's project**, so the request carries `project_id` and the API resolves the project before writing. |

The global store holds *events*; the projection only borrows **read** access to
each project. There is no second copy of task data anywhere.

## 5. Backend API (contract)

All routes live in a new `api/codx/junior/api/calendar.py` exporting `router`
(auto-discovered, mounted at `/api`). Project scope comes from
`request.state.codx_junior_session.settings`, like `meets.py` and `management.py`.

**These routes are global.** They still read `request.state.codx_junior_session`
for authentication — and, for the projection, to know which project to resolve
when a write says `project_id` — but the storage they touch is **not** the
project's `.codx`. Nothing in this router may use `settings.codx_path` as the
data root (`meets.py` and `management.py` do, because their data *is* per project).

### 5.1 Calendars

| Method | Path | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/calendar/calendars` | Only the ones the viewer may see (scope resolution, §11). Includes materialised `system` + `external` entries. |
| `POST` | `/api/calendar/calendars` | `{name, color, scope, audience?, timezone?, default_reminders?}` → 201. `scope: workspace` requires an admin. |
| `PUT` | `/api/calendar/calendars/{id}` | Partial update (name, color, scope, visible, order, reminders, audience). Only the owner (or admin) may. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/calendar/calendars/{id}?move_to={other}` | 409 if it still has events and `move_to` was not given. A `system` calendar returns 409 `read_only_calendar`. |
| `GET` | `/api/calendar/calendars/{id}/share` | `{scope, owner, audience, members[]}` for the sharing panel (teams resolved live). |
| `GET` | `/api/calendar/projects` | The projects the viewer can put events in: `[{project_id, name, role}]`. Feeds the project filter and the editor's project selector. |
| `GET` | `/api/calendar/prefs` · `PUT` | The caller's `prefs/<username>.json` (hidden calendars, order, week start). |

### 5.2 Events and occurrences

| Method | Path | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/api/calendar/events/query` | **The main read**: `{calendar_ids?, from, to, projects?, q?, sources?, include_hidden?}` → `{range, calendars, occurrences[], counts, warnings?}`. Recurrences are expanded server-side. |
| `GET` | `/api/calendar/events/{id}` | Raw event (for the editor, which needs the rule, not the instances). |
| `POST` | `/api/calendar/events` | Create. `calendar_ids[]` required. |
| `PUT` | `/api/calendar/events/{id}` | Update. `If-Match: <revision>`; 409 `revision_mismatch` otherwise. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/calendar/events/{id}?scope=single\|following\|all` | Recurring delete semantics, same three options as Google. |
| `POST` | `/api/calendar/events/{id}/snooze` | `{minutes, occurrence_start}` → reschedules the reminder. |
| `POST` | `/api/calendar/events/quick` | `{text}` → parsed draft (`"Lunch Ana tom 13:00 1h @Café"`), **not persisted** until confirmed. |

Why a `POST /query` instead of `GET /events?from=…`: the request carries arrays
(calendar ids, sources) and grows; `POST` matches the existing
`POST /api/management/tasks/query` and `POST /api/planning/*` convention.

**The project filter (`projects[]`)** — the only dimension D1 adds to the query:

| `projects` | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| absent / `[]` | everything the viewer can see (no project filtering) |
| `["acme-web"]` | items with `project_id == "acme-web"` |
| `["personal"]` | items with `project_id == null` |
| several ids | **OR** of the above, never AND |

The filter is applied *after* visibility and *before* recurrence expansion, and
the same `projects[]` is forwarded to the projection (§4.6), so an unfiltered
month view never reads 30 projects.

**Response sketch**

```json
{
  "range": { "from": "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z", "to": "2026-03-01T00:00:00Z", "timezone": "Europe/Madrid" },
  "calendars": [{ "id": "cal_work", "name": "Work", "color": "#CC0099", "scope": "private", "read_only": false }],
  "projects": ["codx-junior-platform", "acme-web", "personal"],
  "occurrences": [ /* §3.3, each with project_id */ ],
  "counts": { "by_calendar": { "cal_work": 12 }, "by_source": { "task": 5, "native": 7 }, "by_project": { "acme-web": 2 } },
  "warnings": [],
  "truncated_projects": []
}
```

### 5.3 Concurrency, errors and events

- Optimistic locking with `revision` + `If-Match`. Two tabs editing the same
  event: the loser gets `409 revision_mismatch` with the current document so the
  UI can show a diff, instead of silently overwriting.
- Error codes (string `detail` prefix, consistent with `HTTPException` usage
  across the API): `read_only_calendar`, `revision_mismatch`, `event_too_long`,
  `invalid_recurrence`, `unknown_calendar`, `calendar_in_use`.
- After every successful write:
  `emit_collection_event(COLLECTION_CALENDAR_EVENTS, action, {id, calendar_ids}, settings=…)`
  → every open tab reloads only the affected range (new entries added to
  `COLLECTIONS` in `collection_events.py`).

### 5.4 Task → calendar fields

Extend `Chat` (`api/codx/junior/db.py`). All have defaults, so old task files load
unchanged and the existing `POST /api/chats/metadata` path persists them with no
new endpoint:

```python
calendar_ids: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list,
    description="Calendars this task is pinned to, beyond the implicit 'codx-junior' one")
scheduled_start: Optional[str] = None   # ISO datetime, the time block
scheduled_end:   Optional[str] = None   # ISO datetime
all_day: bool = False
```

`due_date` stays a **date** and keeps its meaning (deadline) — the calendar draws
it as an all-day marker with a deadline flag, while `scheduled_start/end` is the
work block. Conflating them would break the overdue logic in
`planning_manager.py`, which is tested and consumed by the Planning view.

## 6. The `codx-junior` calendar (R5 + R6)

A virtual calendar, visible from every project, **read-only**. It is the one thing
that deliberately crosses project boundaries (D1): its items depict **every project
the viewer can open**. Nothing is stored — it is computed on read.

| Source | Rule | Badge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Task with `scheduled_start/end` | Block at that time, in the task's own project. | `Task` |
| Task with `due_date`, no schedule | All-day marker on the due date; `overdue` styling if `due < today` and `status != done`. | `Due` |
| Orchestration run (`run_id`, `run_status`) | Block from `started_at`, or all-day if not started. | `Run` |
| Meet | Block at the scheduled time (needs the new `Meet.scheduled_start`, §11). | `Meet` |

Properties:

- **Not writable.** Dragging a `codx-junior` item moves the *task*, in the project
  that owns it (`PUT /api/planning/tasks/{id}`, resolved from the item's
  `project_id`), not an event. This is the behaviour that makes the calendar
  useful instead of a second task board.
- **Filterable** by project (§5.2), source, board, sprint, assignee and status
  (the query's `projects` + `sources` + `boards` fields), reusing the planning
  filters.
- **Multi-calendar**: a task shows *simultaneously* in `codx-junior` and in any
  calendar in its `calendar_ids`. Adding it to "Work" does not duplicate it; it
  is one task with two memberships, so completing it clears both.
- **Same title, different projects = different items.** Two `project_id`s, two
  chips, and the chip tooltip / agenda row carry the project badge so they are
  never confused.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    T1[Chat / task<br/>project A<br/>scheduled_start, calendar_ids=['cal_work']]
    T2[Chat / task<br/>project B]
    T1 --> P[Projection<br/>projects[] filter, capped]
    T2 --> P
    P --> SYS[codx-junior calendar<br/>system, read-only, all projects]
    P --> W[Work calendar<br/>via calendar_ids]
    W -->|drag / resize| API[PUT /api/planning/tasks/:id<br/>resolved by project_id]
    SYS -->|drag / resize| API
```

## 7. Notifications and popup reminders (R3 + R4)

### 7.1 Pipeline

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant BG as Background thread (30 s)
    participant ST as calendar store
    participant SIO as Socket.IO (broadcast)
    participant CL as Client store/calendar.js
    participant UI as NotificationCentre + popup

    BG->>ST: load events in [now-1d, now+7d]
    BG->>BG: expand occurrences, compute trigger_at = start - minutes
    BG->>ST: read delivered.json
    BG->>BG: due = trigger_at <= now and not delivered
    BG->>ST: append to delivered.json (atomic)
    BG->>SIO: emit codx-junior-calendar-reminder {occurrence, minutes_before}
    SIO->>CL: event
    CL->>UI: push notification + show popup card
    UI->>ST: POST /events/{id}/snooze  (optional)
```

### 7.2 Why a background thread and not "the browser sets a timeout"

The browser timer is the easy path and it is wrong: it dies with the tab, it
cannot deliver when the app is closed, and a laptop asleep at 09:45 never fires
the 10:00 reminder. The server tick also makes email/Web-Push a later plug-in
instead of a rewrite.

It still degrades gracefully: if the tick runs while nobody is connected, the
reminder is **marked delivered and persisted**, so the notification centre shows
it as "missed" the next time the client loads (`GET /api/calendar/reminders?since=`).

### 7.3 Delivery dedupe

`delivered.json`:

```json
{ "evt_01JQ8Z…|2026-02-10T09:00:00Z|15": "2026-02-10T08:45:03Z" }
```

Key = `event_id|occurrence_start|minutes_before`. Bounded: entries older than 30
days are pruned on every tick (≈ 3 events/day → a few hundred lines). Exactly the
same trick as the harness `notification_sent` flag (see
`api/tests/harness/test_harness_notification.py`: "must be sent exactly once …
the durable flag survives duplicate ticks/restarts").

### 7.4 Client side

- `store/calendar.js` (new Vuex module) holds `calendars`, `occurrences`,
  `notifications[]` (**persistent**, unlike `ui.notifications`), `unreadCount`.
- Socket handler registered once at `init()`:
  `API.socket.on('codx-junior-calendar-reminder', …)` (the `SocketManager.on`
  keeps named listeners across reconnects — verified in `api/socket.js`).
- `components/calendar/ReminderPopup.vue` — bottom-right card: title, time,
  "Snooze 5 / 10 min", "Dismiss", "Open". Auto-dismiss after 60 s **without**
  losing the notification-centre entry.
- `components/Notifications.vue` gains a third section ("Reminders") plus
  unread/read state. The transient `ui.addNotification` toasts stay for
  operational messages (they are not a reminder channel).
- Browser `Notification` API: **opt-in** toggle in the calendar settings, used
  only when the tab is backgrounded. Requires HTTPS/localhost.
- M3 extension: Web Push (service worker + VAPID) and email; both plug into the
  same tick, which is why the design keeps delivery out of the request path.

## 8. Recurrence and timezones

### 8.1 Model

Store **RFC 5545 RRULE** as a string, plus exceptions — the same shape Google
Calendar and ICS use, so export is lossless:

```json
"recurrence": {
  "rrule": "FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=1;BYDAY=MO,WE;UNTIL=20260630T000000Z",
  "exdates": ["2026-03-04T09:00:00Z"],
  "overrides": {
    "2026-03-11T09:00:00Z": { "start": "2026-03-11T14:00:00Z", "end": "2026-03-11T15:00:00Z", "title": "Spec review (moved)" }
  }
}
```

`overrides` keys are the *original* occurrence starts, i.e. `RECURRENCE-ID` in
ICS terms — a straight mapping.

### 8.2 Expansion rules (server)

- Expand only inside the requested range, hard-capped at
  `MAX_OCCURRENCES = 750` per event and a 2-year horizon (`invalid_recurrence`
  beyond that).
- Everything is computed in the **event's** timezone, then serialised as UTC.
  This is what makes `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO` stay at 09:00 local across a DST
  change instead of drifting to 08:00/10:00 as a naive UTC expansion does.
- `UNTIL` is inclusive; `COUNT` counts generated instances.

### 8.3 Dependencies (verified)

| Need | Today | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RRULE parsing/expansion (Python) | `python-dateutil` is **not** a declared dependency in `api/pyproject.toml` | Add `python-dateutil>=2.9` (pure-python, MIT, tiny). It ships `dateutil.rrule`, the reference implementation. |
| ICS import/export | not present | Add `icalendar>=6.0` (pure python). Alternatively hand-write the (small) VEVENT/VTIMEZONE subset — decide in M2. |
| Client recurrence | `moment` only (no `moment-timezone`, no `rrule`) | Not needed: the server returns occurrences. |
| Client timezone display | `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in the browser | Use it; no new client dependency. |

> Rule of thumb for this feature: **the browser never does date maths**. It
> formats what the API gives it. That is how the prototype is built too.

│ MY CALENDARS       │  └────┴────┴────┴────┴────┴────┴────┘                 │
│ ☑ Work      (me)   │                                                       │

Two rules of this anatomy, both consequences of the decisions above:

1. **The project filter is the only thing that narrows the agenda** (D1). It sits
   directly under the toolbar, multi-select, with `All` as the default. Changing
   it never reloads a project or changes the URL — the store is global.
2. **The sidebar groups by SCOPE, not by project** (D2): *My calendars* (private),
   *Shared with me* (team + workspace), *codx-junior* (system), *Other*
   (external). A lock/one-person glyph marks private, a people glyph team.

### 9.2 Views

| View | Content | Key interaction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Month** | 6×7 grid, up to 3 chips per day, "+N more" opens the day | click day → create; click chip → detail popover |
| **Week** | 7 columns × 24 h, all-day row on top, overlaps side by side, "now" line | click/drag empty slot → create with prefilled time; drag event → move (optimistic + `PUT`) |
| **Day** | same as week, one column, 15-min slots | resize bottom edge → new `end` |
| **Agenda** | scrollable list grouped by day, 30 days from the cursor, with filters | infinite scroll (reuse the planning pattern: `PAGE_SIZE` + `loadNextPage`) |
| **Sidebar mini** | 6-week mini month, dots per day, click → jump | — |

### 9.3 Interaction rules that matter

1. **Colour = calendar.** A chip's bar uses the primary calendar colour; when the
   item belongs to more than one calendar, the bar becomes a two-tone gradient
   and the tooltip lists them. This is how R6 stays visible without clutter.
2. **Source badge, not colour, marks provenance.** `Task`, `Due`, `Run`, `Meet`
   are small textual badges. Provenance is orthogonal to membership.
3. **Read-only items are visibly different**: no resize handles, an info line
   "Managed by the Task Manager → *open task*".
4. **Optimistic updates.** Move/resize renders instantly and reconciles with the
   server response; on `409 revision_mismatch` the item snaps back with a toast.
5. **Keyboard**: `n` new, `t` today, `m/w/d/a` views, `←/→` navigate, `/` search,
   `Esc` close, `Delete` on a focused chip.
6. **Empty/loading/error**: skeleton grid while the first query resolves; a
   calendar with zero occurrences keeps its colour in the sidebar but draws no
   chips; a shard read error shows a per-day inline warning instead of a blank
   screen.
7. **Mobile**: the month grid becomes the default; day/agenda replace week; the
   sidebar becomes a drawer; "swipe to navigate periods" (the route already has
   `meta.mobile` conventions to follow).

### 9.4 Where the screen lives

Registry work (three lines + one component), following `config/apps.js`:

```js
// config/apps.js
calendar: {
  id: 'calendar', title: 'Calendar', component: 'calendar', icon: 'fa-regular fa-calendar-days',
  route: () => ({ name: 'calendar' })
}
```
```js
// config/appComponentsMap.js
'calendar': lazy(() => import('../views/CalendarView.vue'))
```
```ts
// router/index.ts
{ path: '/:projectName/calendar', name: 'calendar', component: AppRouteView,
  meta: { app: 'calendar', ...mobile('Calendar', 'more') } }
```

That single registration makes it a dockview panel on desktop and a route on
mobile — no branching code.

---

## 10. Interoperability — an explicit non-goal

**Google Calendar is not integrated** (decision D4). It was named in the request
as a *design reference* — the interaction model this document copies — not as a
system to sync with. So, deliberately:

| Not built | Why it stays out |
| --- | --- |
| Google OAuth | No account to link. `security/github_oauth.py` remains the only OAuth implementation. |
| `icalendar` / `python-dateutil` as **required** deps | Both are still absent from `api/pyproject.toml` (verified). If they are ever added it must be for a dated need, not "maybe ICS". |
| Incremental sync, `syncToken`, `watch` channels | The expensive parts of the problem, and they buy nothing until there is an account to sync. |
| Free/busy across accounts, Gmail invitations | Same. |

What is left, optionally and with **zero new dependencies**:

| Optional nice-to-have | Scope | Effort |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **ICS export** (`GET /api/calendar/feed/{calendar_id}.ics?token=…`, token = HMAC of `calendar_id + user`) | Lets a user add their codx-junior calendar to *any* external client (Apple, Thunderbird, Google) without us ever calling an external API. A serialiser for `VEVENT` is ~60 lines. | S |
| **ICS import** (`POST /api/calendar/import`, idempotent by `UID`) | Symmetric, and it validates the `external` scope we already model. | M |

Neither is a milestone. Ship them only if a user asks for a feed; the data model
already supports them (`external` scope, `refs.external_uid`).

---

## 11. Multi-user, permissions, and scheduling meets

Because the store is **global** (D1) and calendars can be **private or shared**
(D2), the ACL is resolved **per request** and never baked into the files.

### 11.1 Who sees which calendar

```
viewer ──▶ for each calendar in calendars.json:
            scope == 'private'   → owner == viewer.username
            scope == 'team'      → membership in audience (team <project>/<name>
                                    resolved live via the team manager)
            scope == 'workspace' → true (any authenticated user)
            scope == 'system'    → true, read_only
            scope == 'external'  → true, read_only
```

| Role in `members[]` | Read | Write / delete | Share |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `owner` | yes | yes | yes (change `scope`/`audience` too) |
| `writer` | yes | yes | no |
| `reader` | yes | **no** (403 `read_only_calendar`) | no |
| not a member | **no** (the calendar is not returned at all) | no | no |
| global admin | yes | yes | yes |

Rules that matter:

- A **private** calendar of another user must never appear in a list, a count, a
  search result or an error message — "not found" and "not allowed" are the same
  404. The fixture asserts this for `marta` and `bob`
  (`expected_visibility`).
- **Events inherit** the ACL of their calendars; `visibility: private` in the
  document masks title ("Private"), description, location and guests for viewers
  who are neither the creator nor a `writer`, while keeping the time slot —
  overlapping meetings stay visible (`expected_private_masking`).
- `system`/`external` calendars are `read_only` for everyone, including admins.
- The reminder thread runs **once for the whole installation** and fans out to the
  recipients of each calendar (§7.1), so a private calendar's reminder goes only
  to its owner.

### 11.2 Scheduling a meet from the calendar (D3)

`Meet` (`api/codx/junior/meets/model.py`) has no `scheduled_start`: it is a *live
room*, not an appointment. Since the calendar **is** the place to schedule a meet,
we add the appointment to it:

```python
# api/codx/junior/meets/model.py — additive, defaulted
scheduled_start: Optional[str] = None
scheduled_end:   Optional[str] = None
calendar_ids:    List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
project_id:      Optional[str] = None
```

and one endpoint that writes both halves in a single transaction:

```
POST /api/meets/schedule   {title, start, end, calendar_ids[], project_id?, guests[]}
  → creates the Meet (scheduled_start/end, calendar_ids)
  → creates the linked CalendarEvent (refs.meet_id, location "Meet /meet/<id>")
  → returns {meet, event}
  → 409 meet_already_scheduled if the meet has scheduled_start already
```

This closes a real weakness rather than adding one: `MeetManager` keeps meets in
`self._meets` (a dict) and **loses them on restart**, so "a meeting at 15:00
tomorrow" is impossible today. After D3 the calendar event is the durable record
and the meet can be rehydrated from it. Deleting the event cancels the schedule
but keeps the meet; deleting the meet deletes the event (`refs.meet_id`).

---

## 12. Performance budgets

| Scenario | Budget |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /events/query` month view (3 shards, 3 calendars, ~500 occurrences) | < 60 ms p95 |
| Same, with 20 recurring events × 750 instances | < 150 ms (cap `MAX_OCCURRENCES`, paginate agenda) |
| Client render month grid | < 16 ms/frame, no re-render on hover (chips are CSS-only) |
| Reminder tick (one thread, whole installation) | < 50 ms; ≤ 7 days of events loaded |
| Socket payload for a reminder | < 2 KB |

Guard rails: the query rejects ranges wider than 92 days (the agenda paginates);
recurrence expansion is capped; `delivered.json` is pruned.

---

## 13. Accessibility

- Grid is a real table-semantics structure (`role="grid"`, `aria-rowcount`,
  cells focusable, arrow-key navigation between days).
- Chips are `<button>` with `aria-label="Spec review, 10:00–11:00, Work"`.
- Colour is never the only signal: every chip also carries its calendar's initial
  or a dot pattern, so the magenta/green pair is distinguishable for
  deuteranopia (the brand palette's magenta↔green pair is a known risky pair —
  verified in `design/tokens/design-tokens.json` `chartSeries`).
- Reminder popup: `role="alert"`, focusable actions, no auto-dismiss when
  `prefers-reduced-motion` + keyboard focus is inside.
- Minimum hit target 32 px in the month grid; 44 px on mobile.

---

## 14. Test strategy

| Level | What |
| --- | --- |
| Unit (Python) | Store round-trip; atomic write under a simulated crash; month-shard boundary; recurrence expansion incl. DST boundary and `COUNT`/`UNTIL`; reminder dedupe across two ticks and a restart. |
| Unit (JS) | Occurrence layout (overlap lanes), chip density ("+N more"), view range maths. |
| API | Query contract with the fixture; `revision_mismatch`; `read_only_calendar`; ACL for a `reader`. |
| Integration | Task with `calendar_ids` shows in two calendars and in `codx-junior`; editing it in the calendar goes through the planning endpoint. |
| E2E (browser profile) | Create a calendar → create an event with a reminder → advance the server clock → assert the popup and the notification centre. |
| Prototype | `02-prototype/index.html` is the visual acceptance artefact for the UX review. |

Fixtures: `03-fixtures/calendar-fixture.json` (version 2) — 6 calendars, 8
events, 3 tasks in 3 different projects, 1 run, 1 scheduled meet. It carries
**five** assertion sets:

| Key | Asserts |
| --- | --- |
| `expected_query` | 12 occurrences in the anchor week, with the recurrence override expanded and every `project_id` intact. |
| `expected_filters` | `projects[]` semantics: `codx-junior-platform` 9, `acme-web` 2, `personal` 1, `acme-web+personal` 3, `internal-wiki` 1, empty 12 = the unfiltered total. |
| `expected_visibility` | The same request as `alice` / `marta` / `jordi` / `bob`: private calendars of another user are never returned, a `reader` cannot write. |
| `expected_private_masking` | A `visibility: private` event keeps its slot but masks title/description/location/guests for other viewers. |
| `expected_reminders` | 5 triggers in the window with their exact `trigger_at` (incl. a task inheriting its calendar's default reminder), 1 occurrence outside it, the `event_id\|occurrence_start\|minutes_before` dedupe key, and per-owner delivery. |

Every total is derived from the data, not copied: the three disjoint project
filters (9 + 2 + 1) add up to the unfiltered 12.
---

## 15. Risks

| # | Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Task projection drifts from the Task Manager | Users see two truths | One single projection function, server-side; the calendar **never** writes task fields except through the planning API. |
| 2 | `due_date` vs `scheduled_*` confusion | Wrong priority/overdue logic | Keep both, document them, draw `due` as an all-day deadline marker (§6). |
| 3 | Reminder duplicates / losses | Trust damage | Persisted dedupe key + restart test; 30 s tick with a `now-1d` look-back window. |
| 4 | Timezone/DST bugs in recurrence | Meetings one hour off | Compute in the event timezone, store UTC, test the DST weekend explicitly. |
| 5 | Unbounded recurrence expansion | Latency spike | `MAX_OCCURRENCES`, 92-day query cap, 2-year horizon. |
| 6 | Scope creep back to Google sync | A milestone becomes unbounded | D4 in §1.1: Google is a non-goal. A pull request that adds an OAuth flow for it is out of scope until a user asks. |
| 7 | Notification fatigue | Users mute everything | Per-calendar reminder defaults, max 2 reminders per event, quiet hours in `settings.json`. |
| 8 | Board/planning regressions | Broken Task Manager | New `Chat` fields are additive with defaults; the planning tests must stay green before merging. |
| 9 | The existing `SolopreneurCalendar.vue` mock confuses readers | Wrong screen maintained | It is deleted/pointed at the real store in M1 (it is mock-only, verified). |

---

## 16. Delivery plan

| Milestone | Content | Acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **M0 — global foundations** (≈ 4–5 days) | `CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH` in `globals.py`; `calendar/store.py` copying `CompanyStore`; `Calendar` with `scope/owner/audience` + per-request ACL; `api/calendar.py` (calendars, prefs, `projects[]` query, events CRUD); `store/calendar.js`; `views/CalendarView.vue` with the **project filter**, month/week/day/agenda and the scope-grouped sidebar. `Chat.calendar_ids/scheduled_*`. | Two users: `marta` never sees `Work`/`Personal`; a team calendar is readable by a `reader` and not writable; switching the project filter changes the counts exactly as `expected_filters`; fixture tests green. |
| **M1 — projection + writes + meets** (≈ 4 days) | `codx-junior` projection across the filtered projects (§4.6, cache + cap), drag & resize writing back through the planning endpoint with `project_id`, `Meet.scheduled_*` + `POST /api/meets/schedule` (D3), editor modal with guests and a project selector. | Dragging a task chip reschedules the task **in its own project**; a scheduled meet appears on the calendar and survives a restart. |
| **M2 — reminders + notifications** (≈ 3 days) | One background ticker for the installation, `delivered.json` per recipient, socket event, notification centre (unread/read/missed), `ReminderPopup.vue`, snooze, opt-in browser notifications. | Reminder fires exactly once, survives a restart, appears in the centre after being missed, and a private calendar's reminder reaches only its owner. |
| **M3 — recurrence** (≈ 4 days) | RRULE + overrides, per-instance edit/delete. | A weekly event keeps 09:00 across the DST change; moving one instance leaves the series intact. |
| **Optional — ICS export/import** (≈ 1 day) | Only if asked (§10). No new mandatory dependency. | A exported `.ics` opens in any client. |

The sequence is deliberate: **M0 has no new dependency and no background work**,
so the global store and the ACL can ship and be evaluated before the projection
and the scheduler exist. Google moved out of the plan entirely (D4).

---

## 17. Decisions closed, and what is still open

The four questions of the first draft are **closed** (§1.1). They changed the
architecture, so they are restated here with what each one unblocked:

| # | Decision | Unblocked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | The calendar is **global**; projects are a **filter** | the global store path (§4.1), `project_id` on every item, `projects[]` in the query (§5.2), the cross-project projection budget (§4.6), the filter bar in the UI (§9.1) |
| D2 | **Private** *and* **team/workspace** calendars | `scope` / `owner` / `audience` (§3.1), the per-request ACL (§11.1), the scope-grouped sidebar (§9.1) |
| D3 | The calendar **schedules meets** | `Meet.scheduled_*` + `POST /api/meets/schedule` (§11.2), which also makes meets survive a restart |
| D4 | **Google is out of scope** | §10 is a documented non-goal; no OAuth and no new mandatory dependency in M0–M2 |

None of them blocks M0 any more. What follows are **smaller, non-blocking**
questions: each already has a default in this document, so M0 can start and they
can be answered while it is built.

| # | Question | Default assumed here | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Do we model **working hours / per-assignee capacity** (Google's model) so the calendar can feed allocation? | **No** in M0: `assignees[]` is a filter, not a capacity. Adding it later changes only the projection (§6), never the store. | product |
| 2 | Is **email / Web-Push** a must for reminders, and is there SMTP already in global settings to reuse? | Popup + notification centre only (M2). The tick is built so a mail or push channel is a plug-in, not a rewrite (§7.4). | product/infra |
| 3 | Who may create a **`workspace`** calendar, and how is "installation admin" determined globally? | Owner or a global admin (§5.1), reusing the existing user/role resolution. | product |
| 4 | **Quiet hours / reminder fatigue** — cap reminders per event, silence overnight? | Max 2 reminders per event, per-calendar defaults, quiet hours per user in `prefs/<username>.json`. | product |
| 5 | Which **project filter** is active on open — `All`, or the last one used? | `All`; the last selection is remembered per user in `prefs`. | UX |
| 6 | **Retention** of notification-centre entries and `delivered.json` keys? | 30 days, pruned on every tick (§7.3). | ops |

One dependency note, verified in the tree: `python-dateutil` is **not** in
`api/pyproject.toml`. With D4 out of scope it is needed only when **M3
(recurrence)** is scheduled — it alone covers RRULE expansion, and it is
pure-Python and MIT-licensed. `icalendar` is not needed at all unless the
optional ICS work of §10 is ever requested.

8. **Recurrence** — *Daily standup* (Mon–Fri) and *Team retro* (monthly) are

9. **Create** — `+ New event`, pick a second calendar under **“Also show in”**, add
   two reminders, and check the multi-colour chip that results.

## 0. TL;DR — the decision

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Scope | **Global (installation-wide)**: a user works on several projects and needs **one** agenda. Projects are a **filter**, never a namespace (D1). |
| Where does the data live? | `<CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH>` (default `/home/codx-junior/calendar`), beside `companies/` and `analytics/` — JSON written atomically, copying `company/store.py`. **Not** inside the project `.codx`, **not** inside chat/board documents. |
| How many calendars? | Unlimited, global. Each has a colour, timezone, default reminders and a **scope**: `private` / `team` / `workspace` (D2). |
| Who sees what? | Resolved per request from `CodxUser` + team membership + calendar ACL. A private calendar never leaks; a `reader` can read a team calendar but not write it (§11). |
| How does a task appear in several calendars? | The **item** owns the list of calendars (`calendar_ids[]`), not the calendar. A task is *always* in the system calendar `codx-junior` and *optionally* pinned to N user calendars. |
| What is the `codx-junior` calendar? | A **virtual, read-only system calendar** whose items project task/run/meet data **from every project the viewer can see**. Computed on read, never stored. |
| How are projects reconciled? | Every event and every projected item carries `project_id` (nullable = personal). The API takes `projects[]`, the UI shows a project filter. Empty filter = all projects. |
| Can the calendar schedule a meet? | **Yes** (D3). A meet scheduled ahead is a calendar event, and `Meet.scheduled_start/end` is the durable record — which also fixes `MeetManager` being in-memory only. |
| Who expands recurrences and timezones? | The **server** returns *occurrences*, not events (precedent: `planning_manager.py` already derives flags/counts server-side). The client only renders. |
| How do reminders fire? | A background thread in `background.py` ticks every 30 s, dedupes through a persisted `delivered.json`, and emits a socket event. The client turns it into a toast + entry in the notification centre. |
| Google Calendar? | **Out of scope** (D4). Google was a design reference, not an integration. §10 is kept as a documented non-goal; ICS export is the only optional escape hatch. |
| Effort | 4 milestones, §16. M0 (global store + private/team calendars + filters + task projection) is the useful 60 %. |

| id | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| R1 | Visualise events and planning in an agenda (day / week / month / agenda list). |
| R2 | Create **multiple calendars** with own colour/visibility (Google Calendar behaviour). |
| R3 | **Notifications section** (a centre, not just a transient toast). |
| R4 | **Popup reminders** before an event starts. |
| R5 | A **`codx-junior` calendar** showing scheduled tasks, meets and orchestration runs. |
| R6 | A **task can belong to several calendars**. |
| R7 | Create, edit, move, resize, delete events; all-day and multi-day events. |
| R8 | Recurring events. |
| R9 | Guests/attendees on an event (at minimum a link to a project user). |
| R10 | Follow Google Calendar interaction conventions so no training is needed. |
| R11 | Must not break the existing Task Manager, Planning view or Meet scheduling. |
| R12 | Deep analysis + prototype **before** any change (this document + prototype). |
| R13 | **Global**: one agenda across every project; projects are a filter, not a namespace. |

| scope | Who sees it | Who writes | `audience` | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `private` | **only `owner`** | `owner` | `null` | "Work", "Personal" |

| `system` | every authenticated user | **nobody** (virtual) | `{kind:"workspace"}` | `codx-junior` |

project control plane (`.codx/teams/`), while the calendar itself is global. That
qualified name is the only coupling between the two worlds — no copying of

## 4. Storage design

### 4.1 Layout

```
${CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH:-/home/codx-junior/calendar}/
├── calendars.json                 # [Calendar]  — small, single document, ALL users
├── events/
│   ├── 2026-01.json               # [CalendarEvent] keyed by start month (UTC)
│   ├── 2026-02.json
│   └── 2026-03.json
├── delivered.json                 # reminder dedupe, per recipient (see §7.3)
├── prefs/<username>.json          # that user's hidden calendars, order, week start
└── export/
    └── cal_work.ics               # generated feed, on demand
```

Three things moved compared with the per-project draft:

| was (per project) | is (global) | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<codx_path>/calendar/` | `$CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH` | `<codx_path>` is `<project>/.codx` (`project_manager.create_project`): one store per project means the same calendar in N places. |
| `settings.json` shared | `prefs/<username>.json` | Visibility and order are **per user**; a shared settings file makes two users fight over one JSON. |
| `export/` git-ignored | generated on request | Nothing is committed anywhere. |

The path goes into `api/codx/junior/globals.py` beside the existing global
folders, so it is overridable in containers and tests:

```python
# Global path for the calendar store, shared across all projects.
CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH = os.environ.get(
    "CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH", "/home/codx-junior/calendar"
)
```

### 4.2 Why not store this on the Chat / board document?

- A board document is rewritten wholesale on every card move; adding events
  there would multiply write amplification and lock contention.
- Events are **not** tasks: they have guests, recurrence and reminders, and they
  must be queryable by date range across the whole project.
- Tasks only ever *project* into the calendar. Keeping the projection read-only
  guarantees that the Task Manager stays the single writer of task data.

**Not inside the project either** (D1). `<codx_path>` is *the project's* `.codx`
(`settings.codx_path = f"{project_path}/.codx"` in `project_manager.py`), so a
per-project store would mean:

- the same "Team — Platform" calendar existing once per project, diverging;
- a reminder firing N times, once per project copy;
- a personal calendar that disappears when you switch project — exactly what the
  requirement rules out.

The precedent already exists twice in the codebase: `ANALYTICS_DATA_PATH` and
`API_LOGS_DATA_PATH` are documented as *"Global path … shared across all projects"*,
and `CODX_JUNIOR_COMPANIES_PATH` keeps hybrid organizations in a global folder.
The calendar joins that family.

### 4.3 Conventions copied from `company/store.py`

`CompanyStore` is the closest existing thing: a **global** root, one document per
entity, atomic write and a per-entity lock. Copy it instead of inventing one.

- **Root resolution**: env var → `codx.junior.globals` → default constant, exactly
  like `get_companies_root()`.
- **Atomic write**: temp file in the same directory → `flush` → `fsync` →
  `os.replace`. A crash can never leave half a month file.
- **Cross-process exclusion**: `fcntl.flock` on `calendar/.lock` while a write is
  in flight (the API runs several uvicorn workers — see the comment in
  `pyproject.toml` about multi-worker deployments), falling back to a thread lock
  when `fcntl` is unavailable, like `CompanyStore.lock`.
- **Bounded, validated ids**: `os.path.basename()` on every id before building a
  path, like `CompanyStore.company_dir`.
- **Tolerant reads**: a corrupt month file is logged and skipped; the calendar
  still renders (never a 500 because of one bad file).

### 4.4 Month sharding and the overlap problem

Query windows are small by nature (month view = 3 shards, week = 2, agenda = 2).
A long event (holiday, offsite) may start before the window and overlap into it.
Rule:

> An event is stored in the shard of its **start** month, and a range query reads
> `[from - MAX_EVENT_DURATION, to]` where `MAX_EVENT_DURATION = 31 days`.
> Events longer than 31 days are rejected on write (400 `event_too_long`); a
> "long" period must be a recurring event or an all-day per-day block.

This keeps every query at ≤ 4 file reads with no index to maintain. The shards
are now **global** (every user, every project), so the threshold arrives sooner:
past ~20 k events add `events/index.json`
(`{id, month, start, end, calendar_ids, project_id}`) — the documented escape
hatch, not part of M0.

### 4.5 Size budget

| Item | Estimate |
| --- | --- |
| Calendar | ~400 B |
| Event (with description) | ~1 KB |
| 2 000 events / year / **installation** | ≈ 2 MB total, ≈ 170 KB per shard |

Comfortably JSON. No database, no migration of existing data.

### 4.6 Cross-project projection cost (the price of D1)

The `codx-junior` calendar is the only part that must look **outside** the global
store, because tasks live in each project's `.codx`. That is the one real cost the
global decision adds, and it is bounded:

| Concern | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Which projects? | `CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH` (`globals.py`) → project folders; keep only those the viewer can open (`CodxUser.projects`, `ProjectPermission`, `children`). Never read a project the viewer cannot access. |
| How many at once? | The projects in the current filter, capped (`MAX_PROJECTS_PER_QUERY = 12`). An unfiltered request projects the 12 most recently touched and says so in the response (`truncated_projects`). |
| Cost per project | Reuse the existing per-project task read (`task_manager` / kanban store). No new file format, no cross-project index. |
| Cache | In-process dict keyed by `(project_id, mtime of its task store)`; an unchanged project is not re-read. Rebuildable, like the `RUNTIME_FOLDER` caches. |
| Failure | A project that fails to read is skipped and reported in `warnings[]`; one broken project never blanks the agenda. |
| Write path | None. Dragging a projected item calls the planning endpoint **in that item's project**, so the request carries `project_id` and the API resolves the project before writing. |

The global store holds *events*; the projection only borrows **read** access to
each project. There is no second copy of task data anywhere.

## 5. Backend API (contract)

All routes live in a new `api/codx/junior/api/calendar.py` exporting `router`
(auto-discovered, mounted at `/api`). Project scope comes from
`request.state.codx_junior_session.settings`, like `meets.py` and `management.py`.

**These routes are global.** They still read `request.state.codx_junior_session`
for authentication — and, for the projection, to know which project to resolve
when a write says `project_id` — but the storage they touch is **not** the
project's `.codx`. Nothing in this router may use `settings.codx_path` as the
data root (`meets.py` and `management.py` do, because their data *is* per project).

### 5.1 Calendars

| Method | Path | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/calendar/calendars` | Only the ones the viewer may see (scope resolution, §11). Includes materialised `system` + `external` entries. |
| `POST` | `/api/calendar/calendars` | `{name, color, scope, audience?, timezone?, default_reminders?}` → 201. `scope: workspace` requires an admin. |
| `PUT` | `/api/calendar/calendars/{id}` | Partial update (name, color, scope, visible, order, reminders, audience). Only the owner (or admin) may. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/calendar/calendars/{id}?move_to={other}` | 409 if it still has events and `move_to` was not given. A `system` calendar returns 409 `read_only_calendar`. |
| `GET` | `/api/calendar/calendars/{id}/share` | `{scope, owner, audience, members[]}` for the sharing panel (teams resolved live). |
| `GET` | `/api/calendar/projects` | The projects the viewer can put events in: `[{project_id, name, role}]`. Feeds the project filter and the editor's project selector. |
| `GET` | `/api/calendar/prefs` · `PUT` | The caller's `prefs/<username>.json` (hidden calendars, order, week start). |

### 5.2 Events and occurrences

| Method | Path | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/api/calendar/events/query` | **The main read**: `{calendar_ids?, from, to, projects?, q?, sources?, include_hidden?}` → `{range, calendars, occurrences[], counts, warnings?}`. Recurrences are expanded server-side. |
| `GET` | `/api/calendar/events/{id}` | Raw event (for the editor, which needs the rule, not the instances). |
| `POST` | `/api/calendar/events` | Create. `calendar_ids[]` required. |
| `PUT` | `/api/calendar/events/{id}` | Update. `If-Match: <revision>`; 409 `revision_mismatch` otherwise. |
| `DELETE` | `/api/calendar/events/{id}?scope=single\|following\|all` | Recurring delete semantics, same three options as Google. |
| `POST` | `/api/calendar/events/{id}/snooze` | `{minutes, occurrence_start}` → reschedules the reminder. |
| `POST` | `/api/calendar/events/quick` | `{text}` → parsed draft (`"Lunch Ana tom 13:00 1h @Café"`), **not persisted** until confirmed. |

Why a `POST /query` instead of `GET /events?from=…`: the request carries arrays
(calendar ids, sources) and grows; `POST` matches the existing
`POST /api/management/tasks/query` and `POST /api/planning/*` convention.

**The project filter (`projects[]`)** — the only dimension D1 adds to the query:

| `projects` | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| absent / `[]` | everything the viewer can see (no project filtering) |
| `["acme-web"]` | items with `project_id == "acme-web"` |
| `["personal"]` | items with `project_id == null` |
| several ids | **OR** of the above, never AND |

The filter is applied *after* visibility and *before* recurrence expansion, and
the same `projects[]` is forwarded to the projection (§4.6), so an unfiltered
month view never reads 30 projects.

**Response sketch**

```json
{
  "range": { "from": "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z", "to": "2026-03-01T00:00:00Z", "timezone": "Europe/Madrid" },
  "calendars": [{ "id": "cal_work", "name": "Work", "color": "#CC0099", "scope": "private", "read_only": false }],
  "projects": ["codx-junior-platform", "acme-web", "personal"],
  "occurrences": [ /* §3.3, each with project_id */ ],
  "counts": { "by_calendar": { "cal_work": 12 }, "by_source": { "task": 5, "native": 7 }, "by_project": { "acme-web": 2 } },
  "warnings": [],
  "truncated_projects": []
}
```

### 5.3 Concurrency, errors and events

- Optimistic locking with `revision` + `If-Match`. Two tabs editing the same
  event: the loser gets `409 revision_mismatch` with the current document so the
  UI can show a diff, instead of silently overwriting.
- Error codes (string `detail` prefix, consistent with `HTTPException` usage
  across the API): `read_only_calendar`, `revision_mismatch`, `event_too_long`,
  `invalid_recurrence`, `unknown_calendar`, `calendar_in_use`.
- After every successful write:
  `emit_collection_event(COLLECTION_CALENDAR_EVENTS, action, {id, calendar_ids}, settings=…)`
  → every open tab reloads only the affected range (new entries added to
  `COLLECTIONS` in `collection_events.py`).

### 5.4 Task → calendar fields

Extend `Chat` (`api/codx/junior/db.py`). All have defaults, so old task files load
unchanged and the existing `POST /api/chats/metadata` path persists them with no
new endpoint:

```python
calendar_ids: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list,
    description="Calendars this task is pinned to, beyond the implicit 'codx-junior' one")
scheduled_start: Optional[str] = None   # ISO datetime, the time block
scheduled_end:   Optional[str] = None   # ISO datetime
all_day: bool = False
```

`due_date` stays a **date** and keeps its meaning (deadline) — the calendar draws
it as an all-day marker with a deadline flag, while `scheduled_start/end` is the
work block. Conflating them would break the overdue logic in
`planning_manager.py`, which is tested and consumed by the Planning view.

## 6. The `codx-junior` calendar (R5 + R6)

A virtual calendar, visible from every project, **read-only**. It is the one thing
that deliberately crosses project boundaries (D1): its items depict **every project
the viewer can open**. Nothing is stored — it is computed on read.

| Source | Rule | Badge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Task with `scheduled_start/end` | Block at that time, in the task's own project. | `Task` |
| Task with `due_date`, no schedule | All-day marker on the due date; `overdue` styling if `due < today` and `status != done`. | `Due` |
| Orchestration run (`run_id`, `run_status`) | Block from `started_at`, or all-day if not started. | `Run` |
| Meet | Block at the scheduled time (needs the new `Meet.scheduled_start`, §11). | `Meet` |

Properties:

- **Not writable.** Dragging a `codx-junior` item moves the *task*, in the project
  that owns it (`PUT /api/planning/tasks/{id}`, resolved from the item's
  `project_id`), not an event. This is the behaviour that makes the calendar
  useful instead of a second task board.
- **Filterable** by project (§5.2), source, board, sprint, assignee and status
  (the query's `projects` + `sources` + `boards` fields), reusing the planning
  filters.
- **Multi-calendar**: a task shows *simultaneously* in `codx-junior` and in any
  calendar in its `calendar_ids`. Adding it to "Work" does not duplicate it; it
  is one task with two memberships, so completing it clears both.
- **Same title, different projects = different items.** Two `project_id`s, two
  chips, and the chip tooltip / agenda row carry the project badge so they are
  never confused.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    T1[Chat / task<br/>project A<br/>scheduled_start, calendar_ids=['cal_work']]
    T2[Chat / task<br/>project B]
    T1 --> P[Projection<br/>projects[] filter, capped]
    T2 --> P
    P --> SYS[codx-junior calendar<br/>system, read-only, all projects]
    P --> W[Work calendar<br/>via calendar_ids]
    W -->|drag / resize| API[PUT /api/planning/tasks/:id<br/>resolved by project_id]
    SYS -->|drag / resize| API
```
